```{julia}
using ForwardDiff   # explicit gradients for Optim (autodiff kwarg pipeline broken in current Optim)

# PrettyTables v3 compatibility shim. v3 dropped `ft_printf` (now
# `fmt__printf`) and requires the `formatters` keyword to be a Vector.
# All call sites in this document use the v2 form
# `formatters = PrettyTables.ft_printf(fmt, cols)`; re-create
# `ft_printf` so it returns a single-element Vector wrapping the new
# `fmt__printf`, accepting either an Int column index or a range.
if !isdefined(PrettyTables, :ft_printf)
    @eval PrettyTables begin
        ft_printf(fmt, cols) =
            [fmt__printf(fmt, collect(cols isa Integer ? (cols:cols) : cols))]
        ft_printf(fmt) = [fmt__printf(fmt)]   # apply to all columns (v2 single-arg)
    end
end

# PrettyTables v3 also renamed the `header` keyword to `column_labels`
# (which must be an `AbstractVector` — a flat vector for one header row,
# or a vector of row-vectors for stacked headers; a Tuple is rejected).
# `_pt_compat` wraps `pretty_table` so the document's v2-style calls keep
# working: it maps `header` → `column_labels` (Tuple → Vector), and
# normalises `formatters` to a flat Vector. All `PrettyTables.pretty_table`
# call sites in the document route through this wrapper. `_PT_REAL` holds
# the real function (no trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves
# it untouched — no recursion).
const _PT_REAL = PrettyTables.pretty_table
function _pt_compat(data; header = nothing, formatters = nothing,
                    body_hlines = nothing, kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    if header !== nothing
        kw[:column_labels] = header isa Tuple ? collect(header) : header
    end
    if formatters !== nothing
        kw[:formatters] =
            formatters isa Function ? [formatters] :
            formatters isa Tuple ?
                collect(Iterators.flatten(
                    x isa Union{AbstractVector,Tuple} ? x : (x,) for x in formatters)) :
                formatters
    end
    # `body_hlines` (v2) has no v3 equivalent — it only drew cosmetic
    # horizontal rules after given rows. Captured here and dropped so the
    # table still renders (without the extra separators). `alignment` and
    # `row_labels` are unchanged in v3 and pass straight through.
    return _PT_REAL(data; kw...)
end

# Optim autodiff compat shim. The installed Optim's `autodiff` kwarg
# rejects the Symbol form `:forward` (it now expects an ADTypes type),
# and even the ADTypes path trips a DifferentiationInterface bug in
# this version. The fix: don't use Optim's autodiff plumbing at all —
# wrap `f` with an explicit ForwardDiff-computed gradient and call the
# 5-arg `optimize(f, g!, x0, method, opts)` form, which doesn't go
# through autodiff. `_optimize_compat` routes every Optim.optimize call
# in the document through this translation; 4-arg calls with
# `autodiff = :forward` are rewritten to the 5-arg gradient form, all
# other shapes pass through. `_OPT_REAL` holds the real function (no
# trailing `(`, so the route-through rewrite leaves it untouched).
const _OPT_REAL = Optim.optimize
function _optimize_compat(args...; kwargs...)
    kw = Dict{Symbol,Any}(kwargs)
    ad = pop!(kw, :autodiff, nothing)
    # If `autodiff = :forward` is requested, build the gradient via
    # ForwardDiff and use the explicit-gradient path. Handles any arg
    # shape where args[1]=f, args[2]=x0 (method/options follow): 3-arg
    # `(f, x0, method)`, 4-arg `(f, x0, method, opts)`, etc.
    if ad isa Symbol && (ad === :forward || ad === :forwarddiff) && length(args) >= 2
        f, x0 = args[1], args[2]
        g!(g, x) = ForwardDiff.gradient!(g, f, x)
        return _OPT_REAL(f, g!, x0, args[3:end]...; kw...)
    end
    return ad === nothing ? _OPT_REAL(args...; kw...) :
                            _OPT_REAL(args...; autodiff = ad, kw...)
end
```

```{julia}
_rawval(x) = hasproperty(x, :value) ? x.value : x  # unwrap ReadStatTables.LabeledValue

function _numeric_vec(col)
    vals = collect(skipmissing(col))
    isempty(vals) && return Float64[]
    T = Base.nonmissingtype(eltype(col))
    T <: Real && return convert(Vector{Float64}, vals)
    try
        return Float64[Float64(_rawval(v)) for v in vals]
    catch
        return nothing  # non-numeric (strings, etc.)
    end
end

"""
Expand a Stata-style varlist pattern against DataFrame columns. Supports:
  * `t*`, `*t`, `*mpg*`, `t?`   — glob wildcards
  * `price-weight`              — range of columns (inclusive, by column order)
  * exact names, Symbols, vectors, and the literal "_all"
"""
function _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    cols = string.(DataFrames.names(df))
    patterns = vars isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [string(vars)] :
               vars isa AbstractVector ? [string(v) for v in vars] :
               [string(v) for v in collect(vars)]

    out = String[]
    for p in patterns
        if p == "_all"
            append!(out, cols)
        elseif occursin('*', p) || occursin('?', p)
            rx = Regex("^" * replace(p, "*" => ".*", "?" => ".") * "\$")
            for c in cols
                occursin(rx, c) && push!(out, c)
            end
        elseif occursin('-', p) && !startswith(p, "-") && !(p in cols)
            parts = split(p, '-', limit=2)
            i = findfirst(==(String(parts[1])), cols)
            j = findfirst(==(String(parts[2])), cols)
            (i === nothing || j === nothing) && error("Unknown variable in range '$p'")
            i, j = minmax(i, j)
            append!(out, cols[i:j])
        else
            push!(out, p)
        end
    end

    seen = Set{String}(); uniq = String[]
    for v in out
        v in seen || (push!(seen, v); push!(uniq, v))
    end
    return Symbol.(uniq)
end

function summarize_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, vars=nothing; detail::Bool=false)
    if vars === nothing
        varlist = Symbol[]
        for n in DataFrames.names(df)
            _numeric_vec(df[!, n]) === nothing || push!(varlist, Symbol(n))
        end
    else
        varlist = _expand_varlist(df, vars)
    end

    rows = []
    for v in varlist
        xraw = _numeric_vec(df[!, v])
        x = xraw === nothing ? Float64[] : xraw
        n = length(x)
        if n == 0
            push!(rows, (; Variable=string(v), Obs=0, Mean=missing,
                           Std=missing, Min=missing, Max=missing))
            continue
        end
        μ  = Statistics.mean(x)
        σ  = n > 1 ? Statistics.std(x) : missing
        base = (; Variable=string(v), Obs=n, Mean=μ, Std=σ,
                  Min=minimum(x), Max=maximum(x))
        if detail
            qs = Statistics.quantile(x, [0.01,0.05,0.10,0.25,0.50,0.75,0.90,0.95,0.99])
            # Stata uses biased moments for skewness/kurtosis
            m2 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^2)
            m3 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^3)
            m4 = Statistics.mean((x .- μ).^4)
            skew = m2 > 0 ? m3 / m2^(3/2) : missing
            kurt = m2 > 0 ? m4 / m2^2     : missing
            push!(rows, merge(base,
                (; p1=qs[1], p5=qs[2], p10=qs[3], p25=qs[4], p50=qs[5],
                   p75=qs[6], p90=qs[7], p95=qs[8], p99=qs[9],
                   Variance = ismissing(σ) ? missing : σ^2,
                   Skewness = skew, Kurtosis = kurt)))
        else
            push!(rows, base)
        end
    end

    # Stata's `summarize, detail` block — one per requested variable.
    if detail
        _g9d(x; w::Int = 9, mx::Int = 7) = begin
            (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
            sig = mx
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            while length(s) > w && sig > 1
                sig -= 1; s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
            end
            0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
        end
        _comma_d(n::Integer) = replace(string(n), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")
        for r in rows
            v = r.Variable
            x = _numeric_vec(df[!, Symbol(v)])
            x === nothing && (println("$v: not numeric"); continue)
            n = length(x); ssorted = sort(x)
            small4 = ssorted[1:min(4, n)]
            large4 = ssorted[max(1, n - 3):n]    # ascending; Stata also shows ascending here
            println()
            println(lpad(v, 36))
            println("-"^61)
            println(lpad("Percentiles", 26),  lpad("Smallest", 16))
            pct = [0.01, 0.05, 0.10, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 0.90, 0.95, 0.99]
            qs  = Statistics.quantile(x, pct)
            sml = [get(small4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            lrg = [get(large4, i, missing) for i in 1:4]
            # Row 1: 1% / small[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "1%",
                           _g9d(qs[1]), _g9d(sml[1]))
            # Row 2: 5% / small[2]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "5%",
                           _g9d(qs[2]), _g9d(sml[2]))
            # Row 3: 10% / small[3]                Obs <N>
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "10%",
                           _g9d(qs[3]), _g9d(sml[3]),
                           "Obs", _comma_d(n))
            # Row 4: 25% / small[4]                Sum of wgt.
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "25%",
                           _g9d(qs[4]), _g9d(sml[4]),
                           "Sum of wgt.", _comma_d(n))
            println()
            # Row 5: 50% / blank          Mean
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "50%",
                           _g9d(qs[5]), "", "Mean", _g9d(r.Mean))
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n",
                           "", "", "Largest",
                           "Std. dev.", _g9d(r.Std))
            # Row 6: 75% / large[1]
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s\n", "75%",
                           _g9d(qs[6]), _g9d(lrg[1]))
            println()
            # Row 7: 90% / large[2]                Variance
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "90%",
                           _g9d(qs[7]), _g9d(lrg[2]),
                           "Variance", _g9d(r.Variance))
            # Row 8: 95% / large[3]                Skewness
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "95%",
                           _g9d(qs[8]), _g9d(lrg[3]),
                           "Skewness", _g9d(r.Skewness))
            # Row 9: 99% / large[4]                Kurtosis
            Printf.@printf("%3s%12s%16s%14s %s\n", "99%",
                           _g9d(qs[9]), _g9d(lrg[4]),
                           "Kurtosis", _g9d(r.Kurtosis))
        end
        return
    end

    # Stata %9.0g: up to 7 sig figs, capped at 9 chars total (so leading "0."
    # for |x|<1 fits), then leading "0" stripped from |x|<1.
    _g9(x; w::Int=9, mx::Int=7) = begin
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return "."
        sig = mx
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        while length(s) > w && sig > 1
            sig -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 ? replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.") : s
    end
    _comma(num::Integer) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println("    Variable |        Obs        Mean    Std. dev.       Min        Max")
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^57)
    for r in rows
        Printf.@printf("%12s |  %9s   %9s   %9s  %9s  %9s\n",
                       r.Variable, _comma(r.Obs),
                       _g9(r.Mean), _g9(r.Std),
                       _g9(r.Min),  _g9(r.Max))
    end
end

"""
    test_stata(model, vars; values=zeros(length(vars)), depvar="docvis", V=nothing)
    test_stata(model; restrictions, depvar="docvis", V=nothing)

Stata-style `test` for ML-based estimators (Poisson, logit, …). Two call
forms:

1. **Simple form** — pass coef name(s) and (optionally) RHS values. Each
   variable is tested = its `values[k]` (default 0). Equivalent to Stata's
   `test female` / `test female private`.

2. **Joint linear-restrictions form** — pass `restrictions = [r1, r2, …]`
   where each `r_i` is a `Pair{Vector{Pair}, Number}` (use a Vector — not a
   Dict — so display ordering is deterministic). Example:

       ["female" => 1.0]                    => 0.0   #  female = 0
       ["private" => 1.0, "chronic" => 1.0] => 1.0   #  private + chronic = 1

   The LHS vector lists `coefname => weight` pairs in the order they should
   appear in the printed equation; the pair value is the RHS. Equivalent to
   Stata's `test (female) (private + chronic = 1)`. Display strings are
   auto-generated to match Stata's exact format (`[depvar]name`, sign-aware
   coefficients, `+`/`-` joiners).

`V` overrides `vcov(model)` — pass the robust V from `poisson_stata` /
`setup_mus10().V_robust` to match Stata's `test` after `vce(robust)`.
"""
function test_stata(model=nothing, vars=nothing; values=nothing,
                    depvar::AbstractString="docvis",
                    V=nothing, restrictions=nothing,
                    mtest::Bool=false,
                    β=nothing, coefnames=nothing)
    # `β`, `V`, `coefnames` overrides let you test NB / GMM / quantile-
    # regression / bootstrap-derived coefficients without a Stata-style
    # model object — pass `model = nothing`. The first non-nothing source
    # for β / V / coefnames is used (so `test_stata(model)` still works).
    β     = β === nothing ? StatsBase.coef(model) : collect(β)
    Vmat  = V === nothing ? Matrix(StatsBase.vcov(model)) : Matrix(V)
    names = coefnames === nothing ? string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model)) :
                                    string.(coefnames)
    p_idx(v) = (i = findfirst(==(string(v)), names);
                i === nothing && error("'$(v)' not in coefnames=$(names)");
                i)

    # Build R (q × k), r (q-vector), and a display label for each restriction.
    # The LHS of each restriction is a Vector of `coefname => weight` pairs
    # (we accept Dict too for convenience, but ordering is unspecified).
    if restrictions !== nothing
        q = length(restrictions); k = length(β)
        R = zeros(q, k); r = zeros(q); labels = String[]
        for (row, restr) in enumerate(restrictions)
            coefs, rhs = restr.first, restr.second
            pairs = coefs isa AbstractDict ? collect(coefs) : collect(coefs)
            # Build display terms with Stata-style sign handling:
            #   first positive  →  "[depvar]name"
            #   first negative  →  "- [depvar]name"   (space after `-`)
            #   later positive  →  "+ [depvar]name"
            #   later negative  →  "- [depvar]name"
            # Coefficients with |c| ≠ 1 get a "c*" prefix on the symbol.
            term_strs = String[]
            for (idx, (vname, c)) in enumerate(pairs)
                R[row, p_idx(vname)] = float(c)
                cf      = float(c)
                abs_c   = abs(cf)
                core    = abs_c == 1.0 ? "[$depvar]$vname" :
                          Printf.@sprintf("%g*[%s]%s", abs_c, depvar, vname)
                sign_op = cf < 0 ? "-" : "+"
                if idx == 1
                    push!(term_strs, cf < 0 ? "- $core" : core)
                else
                    push!(term_strs, "$sign_op $core")
                end
            end
            r[row] = float(rhs)
            push!(labels, join(term_strs, " ") *
                          " = " * Printf.@sprintf("%g", r[row]))
        end
    else
        vs   = vars isa AbstractVector ? string.(vars) : [string(vars)]
        vals = values === nothing ? zeros(length(vs)) : collect(values)
        q = length(vs); k = length(β)
        R = zeros(q, k); r = vals
        labels = String[]
        # When `depvar` is empty (e.g. testing differences from a bootstrap
        # of an estimator without a single dependent variable), omit the
        # `[depvar]` prefix entirely — matches Stata's behavior for tests
        # on stored vectors with no equation label.
        for (row, v) in enumerate(vs)
            R[row, p_idx(v)] = 1.0
            prefix = isempty(depvar) ? "" : "[$depvar]"
            push!(labels, "$prefix$v = " * Printf.@sprintf("%g", vals[row]))
        end
    end

    Rβ_r = R * β .- r
    chi2 = (Rβ_r' * (LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(R * Vmat * R') \ Rβ_r))::Float64
    df   = size(R, 1)
    pval = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(df), chi2)
    println()
    for (k_, lab) in enumerate(labels)
        Printf.@printf(" ( %d)  %s\n", k_, lab)
    end
    if mtest
        # `mtest` mode (Stata `test ..., mtest`): each row tested in isolation
        # plus the joint test, in a single table. Default is unadjusted p-values
        # — the matching Stata footnote prints "* Unadjusted p-values".
        chi2_each = [let row = R[i:i, :]; rb = row * β .- r[i:i];
                         (rb' * (LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(row * Vmat * row') \ rb))::Float64
                     end for i in 1:df]
        p_each = [1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), c) for c in chi2_each]
        println()
        println("-"^38)
        Printf.@printf("%6s |  %10s  %5s  %9s\n", "", "chi2", "df", "p > chi2")
        println("-"^7, "+", "-"^30)
        for i in 1:df
            Printf.@printf("   (%d) |  %10.2f  %5d  %9.4f*\n",
                           i, chi2_each[i], 1, p_each[i])
        end
        println("-"^7, "+", "-"^30)
        Printf.@printf("%6s |  %10.2f  %5d  %9.4f\n", "All", chi2, df, pval)
        println("-"^38)
        println("* Unadjusted p-values")
    else
        Printf.@printf("\n           chi2(%3d) = %7.2f\n", df, chi2)
        Printf.@printf("         Prob > chi2 = %9.4f\n", pval)
    end
    return (; chi2=chi2, df=df, p=pval)
end

"""
    setup_mus10(df10=nothing; vars=nothing, formula=nothing,
                vce=:robust, quiet=true) -> NamedTuple

Universal helper for any chapter that uses the mus10 dataset (`mus10data.dta`,
filtered to `year02 == 1`). Loads the data internally if `df10` is omitted,
drops missings on `vars`, fits Poisson via `poisson_stata`, and returns a
NamedTuple covering everything downstream chunks need — both **Stata-display
order** (`β`, `V`, `X` — slopes first, `_cons` last; for margins / dydx /
lincom / nlcom helpers) and **GLM order** (`model`, `V_robust = fit.V_glm`;
for `test_stata` and other helpers that go through `coefnames(model)`).

Because the helper auto-loads when `df10` is `nothing`, **any chapter chunk
can call `s = setup_mus10()` without first running a chapter-10 data-load
chunk** — i.e. running just chunk 1 + any chapter chunk works.

Defaults:
  - `vars`    = `[:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income, :age]`
                (chapter 10 / 11 set; pass an explicit shorter list for
                chapter-12 Wald tests where `:age` isn't a regressor)
  - `formula` = `docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income`
  - `vce`     = `:robust`
  - `quiet`   = `true` (set `false` to print the regression table)

Examples (indented for clarity):
    s = setup_mus10()                           # load + fit, default 6 vars
    s = setup_mus10(; quiet = false)            # also print the table
    s = setup_mus10(df10)                       # reuse an already-loaded df10
    s = setup_mus10(; vars = [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income])
"""
function setup_mus10(df10=nothing;
                    vars=nothing, formula=nothing,
                    vce::Symbol=:robust, quiet::Bool=true)
    if df10 === nothing
        df10 = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
        # Promote any non-Float64 numeric / LabeledValue columns to plain
        # Float64 so downstream `Float64.(col)` calls don't trip over
        # ReadStatTables' LabeledValue wrapper.
        for c in DataFrames.names(df10)
            col = df10[!, c]
            T   = eltype(col)
            if T <: Union{Missing, Float64}
                continue
            elseif T <: Union{Missing, Float32, Int}
                df10[!, c] = convert.(Union{Missing, Float64}, col)
            else
                # Catch-all: unwrap LabeledValue or any other wrapper via _rawval.
                df10[!, c] = [ismissing(x) ? missing : Float64(_rawval(x))
                              for x in col]
            end
        end
        df10 = DataFrames.filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df10)
    end
    cols = vars === nothing ?
        [:docvis, :private, :chronic, :female, :income, :age] : vars
    fml  = formula === nothing ?
        GLM.@formula(docvis ~ private + chronic + female + income) : formula
    df10c = DataFrames.dropmissing(df10[:, cols])
    fit = poisson_stata(df10c, fml; vce = vce, quiet = quiet)
    return (; df = df10c, fit,
              model = fit.model, V_robust = fit.V_glm,
              β = fit.β, V = fit.V, X = fit.X,
              n = fit.n, k = fit.k, coefnames = fit.coefnames,
              coefnames_glm = fit.coefnames_glm)
end

"""
    regress_stata(model; level=0.95)

Stata-style `regress` output — prints the ANOVA table, overall F-statistic,
R², adjusted R², Root MSE, and the coefficient table with t-statistics,
p-values, and confidence intervals, matching the format of Stata's
`regress` command. The intercept is relabelled `_cons`.

Works with any `StatsBase`-compatible OLS model, e.g. the output of
`FixedEffectModels.reg(df, @formula(y ~ x2 + x3))`.
"""
function regress_stata(model; level::Float64=0.95, noheader::Bool=false)
    β      = StatsBase.coef(model)
    V      = StatsBase.vcov(model)
    se     = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    nm_raw = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(model))
    nm     = replace.(nm_raw, "(Intercept)" => "_cons")
    has_int = any(==("_cons"), nm)

    n      = Int(StatsBase.nobs(model))
    rss    = StatsBase.deviance(model)
    r2     = StatsBase.r2(model)
    ar2    = StatsBase.adjr2(model)
    dof_r  = Int(StatsBase.dof_residual(model))
    k      = length(β) - (has_int ? 1 : 0)
    tss    = rss / max(1 - r2, eps())
    mss    = tss - rss
    rmse   = sqrt(rss / dof_r)
    Fstat  = (mss / k) / (rss / dof_r)
    pF     = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(k, dof_r), Fstat)

    yname = try
        string(StatsBase.responsename(model))
    catch
        hasproperty(model, :yname) ? string(model.yname) : "y"
    end

    t_stat = β ./ se
    tcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    p_val  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), abs.(t_stat)))
    ci_lo  = β .- tcrit .* se
    ci_hi  = β .+ tcrit .* se

    # Stata %10.0g-style: `sig` significant digits, strip leading 0 for |x|<1,
    # right-aligned in width `w`.
    function _g(x, w; sig=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, ".")
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return Printf.@sprintf("%*s", w, s)
    end

    # ── ANOVA table + summary-stats block (skipped when `noheader=true`,
    # matching Stata's `regress y x, noheader` option)
    if !noheader
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s %10s %10s    %-13s = %10d\n",
                       "Source", "SS", "df", "MS", "Number of obs", n)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.2f", "F($k, $dof_r)", Fstat))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Model", _g(mss, 10), k, _g(mss/k, 10), "Prob > F", pF)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Residual", _g(rss, 10), dof_r, _g(rss/dof_r, 10),
                       "R-squared", r2)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^34, "   ",
                Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %10.4f", "Adj R-squared", ar2))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s %10d %s    %-13s = %10.4f\n",
                       "Total", _g(tss, 10), n-1, _g(tss/(n-1), 10),
                       "Root MSE", rmse)
    end
    println()

    # ── Coefficient table
    println("-"^78)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s  %9s  %6s  %5s     [%d%% conf. interval]\n",
                   yname, "Coefficient", "Std. err.", "t", "P>|t|",
                   round(Int, 100*level))
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for i in eachindex(β)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %6.2f  %5.3f  %s  %s\n",
                       nm[i],
                       _g(β[i], 10),
                       _g(se[i], 9),
                       t_stat[i],
                       p_val[i],
                       _g(ci_lo[i], 11),
                       _g(ci_hi[i], 11))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    return nothing
end

"""
    regress_stata(df, y, xs; level=0.95, vcov=nothing)

Convenience method: fit `y ~ xs…` on `df` with `FixedEffectModels.reg` and
print the Stata-style `regress` output. `y` is the dependent variable (Symbol
or String); `xs` is a Symbol, String, or vector of regressor names. Pass
`vcov=Vcov.robust()` (or similar) for non-default standard errors.

Example:

    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3])
    regress_stata(df5, :y, [:x2, :x3]; vcov=Vcov.robust())
"""
function regress_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, y, xs;
                       level::Float64=0.95, vcov=nothing, weights=nothing,
                       noheader::Bool=false)
    ys  = Symbol(y)
    xsv = xs isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ? [Symbol(xs)] :
          [Symbol(v) for v in xs]
    f = term(ys) ~ sum(term.(xsv))
    kw = weights === nothing ? (;) : (; weights=Symbol(weights))
    m = vcov === nothing ?
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f; kw...) :
        FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f, vcov; kw...)
    regress_stata(m; level=level, noheader=noheader)
    return nothing
end

"""
    ivregress_2sls(df, y, endog => instruments, exog=Symbol[];
                   robust=true, level=0.95, first=true)

Stata-style `ivregress 2sls y (endog = iv) x2list[, vce(robust) first]`.
Runs the model through `FixedEffectModels.reg`:
  * first stage: each endogenous variable regressed on `exog + instruments`
    (plain OLS with robust SE), printed with the familiar
    "Linear regression" header (F, R², Adj R², Root MSE, t-stats);
  * 2SLS:  `reg(df, @formula(y ~ exog + (endog ~ instruments)), vce)`,
    printed with Wald χ², R², Root MSE, z-stats, and Endogenous/Exogenous
    footer.

`endog => instruments` is a Pair where each side is a Symbol or vector of
Symbols. The endogenous variable is placed first in the 2SLS coefficient
table (matching Stata's convention); `_cons` is shown last.

Example:

    ivregress_2sls(df6, :ldrugexp, :hi_empunion => :ssiratio,
                   [:totchr, :age, :female, :blhisp, :linc];
                   robust=true, first=true)
"""
function ivregress_2sls(df, y, endog_iv::Pair, exog=Symbol[];
                        robust::Bool=true, level::Float64=0.95,
                        first::Bool=true)
    ys        = Symbol(y)
    endog     = endog_iv.first isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ?
                [Symbol(endog_iv.first)] :
                [Symbol(v) for v in endog_iv.first]
    iv        = endog_iv.second isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ?
                [Symbol(endog_iv.second)] :
                [Symbol(v) for v in endog_iv.second]
    exog_v    = isempty(exog) ? Symbol[] :
                (exog isa Union{Symbol,AbstractString} ?
                    [Symbol(exog)] : [Symbol(v) for v in exog])
    vcov      = robust ? FixedEffectModels.Vcov.robust() :
                         FixedEffectModels.Vcov.simple()
    _fmtn(x)  = replace(string(x), r"(\d)(?=(\d{3})+$)" => s"\1,")

    # Printer shared by the first-stage (OLS, t) and 2SLS (z) blocks.
    function _print(m, depname; mode::Symbol, endog_nms=nothing)
        β      = StatsBase.coef(m)
        V      = StatsBase.vcov(m)
        se     = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
        nm_raw = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(m))
        nm     = replace.(nm_raw, "(Intercept)" => "_cons")
        n      = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m))
        k      = length(β)
        dof_r  = Int(StatsBase.dof_residual(m))
        rss    = StatsBase.deviance(m)
        r2     = StatsBase.r2(m)
        rmse   = sqrt(rss / dof_r)

        cons_idx = findfirst(==("_cons"), nm)
        slope    = cons_idx === nothing ? collect(1:k) :
                    setdiff(1:k, [cons_idx])
        q        = length(slope)
        Wstat    = β[slope]' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V[slope, slope]) * β[slope]

        lvl = round(Int, 100 * level)

        if mode == :first
            Fstat = Wstat / q
            pF    = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(q, dof_r), Fstat)
            ar2   = 1 - (1 - r2) * (n - 1) / dof_r
            Printf.@printf("%-56s%-14s= %6s\n",  "", "Number of obs", _fmtn(n))
            Printf.@printf("%-56s%-14s= %6.2f\n","", "F($q, $dof_r)", Fstat)
            Printf.@printf("%-56s%-14s= %6.4f\n","", "Prob > F",      pF)
            Printf.@printf("%-56s%-14s= %6.4f\n","", "R-squared",     r2)
            Printf.@printf("%-56s%-14s= %6.4f\n","", "Adj R-squared", ar2)
            Printf.@printf("%-56s%-14s= %6.4f\n","", "Root MSE",      rmse)
            println()

            t_stat = β ./ se
            tcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(dof_r),
                                            1 - (1 - level) / 2)
            pvals  = 2 .* (1 .-
                     Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(dof_r), abs.(t_stat)))
            ci_lo  = β .- tcrit .* se
            ci_hi  = β .+ tcrit .* se
            order  = cons_idx === nothing ? slope : vcat(slope, cons_idx)

            coef_df = DataFrames.DataFrame(
                Variable    = nm[order],
                Coefficient = β[order],
                StdErr      = se[order],
                t           = t_stat[order],
                p           = pvals[order],
                CI_low      = ci_lo[order],
                CI_high     = ci_hi[order],
            )
            _pt_compat(coef_df;
                header = (["",         "",            "Robust",    "",  "",      "",                "" ],
                          [depname,    "Coefficient", "std. err.", "t", "P>|t|",
                           "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"]),
                formatters = vcat(
                    PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.7f", [2, 3, 6, 7]),
                    PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.2f", [4]),
                    PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.3f", [5]),
                ),
                alignment = [:l, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r],
            )
        else        # :second — 2SLS
            pW = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(q), Wstat)
            Printf.@printf("%-50s%-16s= %10s\n",
                           "Instrumental-variables 2SLS regression",
                           "Number of obs", _fmtn(n))
            Printf.@printf("%-50s%-16s= %10.2f\n", "", "Wald chi2($q)", Wstat)
            Printf.@printf("%-50s%-16s= %10.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2",   pW)
            Printf.@printf("%-50s%-16s= %10.4f\n", "", "R-squared",     r2)
            Printf.@printf("%-50s%-16s= %10.4f\n", "", "Root MSE",      rmse)
            println()

            z_stat = β ./ se
            zcrit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(),
                                            1 - (1 - level) / 2)
            pvals  = 2 .* (1 .-
                     Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_stat)))
            ci_lo  = β .- zcrit .* se
            ci_hi  = β .+ zcrit .* se

            # Put endogenous vars first, then the rest of the slopes, then _cons.
            endog_pos = Int[]
            if endog_nms !== nothing
                for ev in endog_nms
                    i = findfirst(==(string(ev)), nm)
                    i !== nothing && push!(endog_pos, i)
                end
            end
            rest = setdiff(slope, endog_pos)
            order = cons_idx === nothing ?
                    vcat(endog_pos, rest) :
                    vcat(endog_pos, rest, cons_idx)

            coef_df = DataFrames.DataFrame(
                Variable    = nm[order],
                Coefficient = β[order],
                StdErr      = se[order],
                z           = z_stat[order],
                p           = pvals[order],
                CI_low      = ci_lo[order],
                CI_high     = ci_hi[order],
            )
            _pt_compat(coef_df;
                header = (["",         "",            "Robust",    "",  "",      "",                "" ],
                          [depname,    "Coefficient", "std. err.", "z", "P>|z|",
                           "[$(lvl)% CI low]", "[$(lvl)% CI high]"]),
                formatters = vcat(
                    PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.7f", [2, 3, 6, 7]),
                    PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.2f", [4]),
                    PrettyTables.ft_printf("%.3f", [5]),
                ),
                alignment = [:l, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r, :r],
            )
        end
    end

    # ── First-stage regressions
    first_stage_models = Any[]
    if first
        println("First-stage regressions")
        println("-"^23)
        println()
        rhs = vcat(exog_v, iv)
        for ev in endog
            f_fs = term(ev) ~ sum(term.(rhs))
            m_fs = FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f_fs, vcov)
            _print(m_fs, string(ev); mode=:first)
            println()
            push!(first_stage_models, m_fs)
        end
    end

    # ── 2SLS (build the IV formula dynamically via @formula + Meta.parse)
    exog_part  = isempty(exog_v) ? "1" : join(string.(exog_v), " + ")
    endog_part = join(string.(endog), " + ")
    iv_part    = join(string.(iv), " + ")
    fmla_str   = "@formula($(string(ys)) ~ $exog_part + ($endog_part ~ $iv_part))"
    f_iv       = Base.eval(@__MODULE__, Meta.parse(fmla_str))
    m_iv       = FixedEffectModels.reg(df, f_iv, vcov)
    _print(m_iv, string(ys); mode=:second, endog_nms=endog)
    Printf.@printf("Endogenous: %s\n", join(string.(endog), " "))
    Printf.@printf("Exogenous:  %s\n",
                   join(string.(vcat(exog_v, iv)), " "))

    return (; first_stage=first_stage_models, iv=m_iv)
end

"""
    poisson_boot_stata(df, formula; B=400, seed=10101, level=0.95, quiet=false)

Stata-style `poisson <depvar> <regs>, vce(bootstrap, reps(B) seed(s))`.
Fits Poisson on `df`, then runs `B` observation-level bootstrap replicates
to estimate the variance of β̂. Prints the full Stata bootstrap table:

  - Header: Number of obs / Replications / Wald chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 /
    Log likelihood / Pseudo R²
  - Coefficient rows in Stata-display order (slopes first, _cons last) with
    "Observed coefficient | Bootstrap std. err. | z | P>|z| | Normal-based
    [95% CI]" — the asymmetric-SE-source notation Stata uses for
    bootstrap-VCE output. CIs are normal-based: β̂ ± 1.96·SE_boot.

Returns `(; β, se, V, β_boot, model, n, B)`.
"""
function poisson_boot_stata(df, formula; B::Int=400, seed::Int=10101,
                            level::Float64=0.95, quiet::Bool=false,
                            cluster_var=nothing, noheader::Bool=false)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    cols   = cluster_var === nothing ? needed : vcat(needed, [Symbol(cluster_var)])
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    m   = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β̂   = GLM.coef(m); cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n   = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m)); k = length(β̂)
    ll  = GLM.loglikelihood(m)

    # Pseudo R² from intercept-only Poisson
    fml_null = StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1)
    m_null   = GLM.glm(fml_null, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)

    # Bootstrap β-matrix (B × k). With `cluster_var`, resample CLUSTERS (Stata's
    # `vce(boot, cluster(varname))`); otherwise plain row-level bootstrap.
    n_clusters = cluster_var === nothing ? 0 :
                 length(unique(dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]))
    β_boot = if cluster_var === nothing
        obs_bootstrap(dfc; B = B, seed = seed, verbose = false) do d
            GLM.coef(GLM.glm(formula, d, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink()))
        end
    else
        panel_bootstrap(dfc, Symbol(cluster_var); B = B, seed = seed,
                        verbose = false) do d
            GLM.coef(GLM.glm(formula, d, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink()))
        end
    end
    V  = Statistics.cov(β_boot)
    se = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V))

    # Wald chi² of slopes-only against zero
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    βs = β̂[slope_idx]; Vs = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
    Wald   = (βs' * (LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(Vs) \ βs))::Float64
    Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), Wald)

    # SE-derived inference
    z      = β̂ ./ se
    pv     = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit   = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo  = β̂ .- crit .* se
    ci_hi  = β̂ .+ crit .* se

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        if !noheader
            # Header (Stata's `bootstrap, noheader:` skips this entire block)
            println()
            Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                           "Poisson regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6s\n", "", "Replications", commafmt(B))
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                           "Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", Wald)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", Wald_p)
            # Right-align the "Pseudo R2 = …" block at col 78, regardless of
            # how many digits "Log likelihood = …" prints on the left.
            ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("Log likelihood = %.5f", ll)
            r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
            pad    = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
            println(ll_str, " "^pad, r2_str)
            println()

            # Cluster-bootstrap info line: right-aligned at col 78,
            # matching Stata's "(Replications based on G clusters in <var>)".
            if cluster_var !== nothing
                cl_str = Printf.@sprintf("(Replications based on %d clusters in %s)",
                                         n_clusters, cluster_var)
                println(lpad(cl_str, 78))
            end
        end

        # Coefficient table — Stata bootstrap layout
        println("-"^78)
        println("             |   Observed   Bootstrap                         ",
                "Normal-based")
        Printf.@printf("%12s | coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β̂[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", pv[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    return (; β = β̂, se, V, β_boot, model = m, n, B)
end

"""
    poisson_boot_ci_stata(df, formula; B=999, seed=10101, level=0.95, quiet=false)

Stata-style `poisson, vce(boot, reps(B) seed(s) bca); estat bootstrap, all`.
Computes ALL FOUR bootstrap CI types per coefficient:

  - **N**   Normal:    β̂ ± z_{α/2} · σ_boot
  - **P**   Percentile: [Q_{α/2}(β_boot), Q_{1−α/2}(β_boot)]
  - **BC**  Bias-corrected:
      z₀ = Φ⁻¹(P(β_boot < β̂))
      lo = Q(Φ(2z₀ − z_{α/2})), hi = Q(Φ(2z₀ + z_{α/2}))
  - **BCa** Bias-corrected and accelerated:
      additionally needs acceleration `a` from leave-one-out jackknife:
      a = Σ(β̄_jack − β_jack(i))³ / [6·(Σ(β̄_jack − β_jack(i))²)^{3/2}]
      lo = Q(Φ(z₀ + (z₀−z_{α/2})/(1−a(z₀−z_{α/2}))))   (similar for hi)

Prints the Stata `estat bootstrap, all` table (Observed coef / Bias /
Bootstrap SE / four CI rows per coefficient with N/P/BC/BCa labels) and
returns a NamedTuple with all components.

Note: BCa adds an O(n) jackknife pass on top of B bootstrap reps. For
n=50 and B=999 this is fast (<1 s); for larger n consider B≥1000 anyway.
"""
function poisson_boot_ci_stata(df, formula; B::Int=999, seed::Int=10101,
                               level::Float64=0.95, quiet::Bool=false)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    m   = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β̂   = GLM.coef(m); cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n   = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m)); k = length(β̂)

    β_boot = obs_bootstrap(dfc; B = B, seed = seed, verbose = false) do d
        GLM.coef(GLM.glm(formula, d, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink()))
    end                                              # B × k
    se_b = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(Statistics.cov(β_boot)))
    bias = vec(Statistics.mean(β_boot, dims = 1)) .- β̂

    # Jackknife (leave-one-out) for BCa acceleration
    β_jack = zeros(n, k)
    for i in 1:n
        sub = dfc[setdiff(1:n, i), :]
        β_jack[i, :] = GLM.coef(GLM.glm(formula, sub,
                                        Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink()))
    end

    α   = 1 - level
    zα2 = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - α/2)
    cis = Vector{Vector{NTuple{2, Float64}}}(undef, k)   # cis[j] = [(N), (P), (BC), (BCa)]
    z0_v = zeros(k); a_v = zeros(k)
    for j in 1:k
        b̂  = β̂[j]
        bj = β_boot[:, j]
        # Normal
        N_lo = b̂ - zα2 * se_b[j]; N_hi = b̂ + zα2 * se_b[j]
        # Percentile
        P_lo = Statistics.quantile(bj, α/2); P_hi = Statistics.quantile(bj, 1 - α/2)
        # BC
        p_lt = sum(bj .< b̂) / B
        # Clamp p_lt away from 0/1 to avoid ±Inf z0 (degenerate corner cases)
        p_lt_safe = clamp(p_lt, 1/(2B), 1 - 1/(2B))
        z0 = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), p_lt_safe)
        BC_lo_p = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), 2*z0 - zα2)
        BC_hi_p = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), 2*z0 + zα2)
        BC_lo = Statistics.quantile(bj, BC_lo_p)
        BC_hi = Statistics.quantile(bj, BC_hi_p)
        # BCa: acceleration from jackknife
        bjk = β_jack[:, j]
        b̄jk = Statistics.mean(bjk)
        d   = b̄jk .- bjk
        a   = sum(d .^ 3) / (6 * (sum(d .^ 2)) ^ 1.5)
        BCa_lo_p = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(),
                                     z0 + (z0 - zα2) / (1 - a*(z0 - zα2)))
        BCa_hi_p = Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(),
                                     z0 + (z0 + zα2) / (1 - a*(z0 + zα2)))
        BCa_lo = Statistics.quantile(bj, BCa_lo_p)
        BCa_hi = Statistics.quantile(bj, BCa_hi_p)
        cis[j] = [(N_lo, N_hi), (P_lo, P_hi), (BC_lo, BC_hi), (BCa_lo, BCa_hi)]
        z0_v[j] = z0; a_v[j] = a
    end

    # Bootstrap-CI table uses higher precision than the standard `poisson_stata`
    # output: Stata shows up to 8 sig figs (e.g. ".98330144"), so the cap is
    # 10/11 chars (sign-aware) and the default sig is 8.
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=8)
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 11 : 10
        sig_use = sig
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        nstr = commafmt(n); bstr = commafmt(B)
        # Stata's `estat bootstrap, all` header uses an 18-char left-padded
        # label ("Number of obs     ", "Replications      ") and a 10-char
        # right-aligned value, separated by " = ".
        Printf.@printf("%-48s%-18s= %10s\n",
                       "Poisson regression", "Number of obs", nstr)
        Printf.@printf("%48s%-18s= %10s\n", "", "Replications", bstr)
        println()

        intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
        slope_idx     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])

        println("-"^78)
        println("             |    Observed               Bootstrap")
        Printf.@printf("%12s | coefficient       Bias    std. err.  [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        labels = ["(N)", "(P)", "(BC)", "(BCa)"]
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            for r in 1:4
                lo, hi = cis[i][r]
                if r == 1
                    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s   %s  %4s\n",
                                   label, g9(β̂[i]; w=10), g9(bias[i]; w=8),
                                   g9(se_b[i]; w=9), g9(lo; w=9),
                                   g9(hi; w=8), labels[r])
                else
                    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s   %s  %4s\n",
                                   "", " "^10, " "^8, " "^9,
                                   g9(lo; w=9), g9(hi; w=8), labels[r])
                end
            end
        end
        println("-"^78)
        println("Key:   N: Normal")
        println("       P: Percentile")
        println("      BC: Bias-corrected")
        println("     BCa: Bias-corrected and accelerated")
    end

    return (; β = β̂, bias, se = se_b, β_boot, β_jack, cis, z0 = z0_v, a = a_v)
end

"""
    poisson_boot_b_se_stata(df, formula; B=400, seed=10101, level=0.95, quiet=false)

Stata-style `bootstrap _b _se, reps(B) seed(s): poisson <depvar> <regs>`.
On each resample, refits Poisson and saves BOTH the coefficient vector β
AND the OIM standard error vector se(β) — so the bootstrap distribution
covers the SE-of-SE as well as the SE-of-β. Prints a two-block table:

  - **docvis block**: bootstrap of β. Observed = original β̂; Bootstrap
    std. err. = std(β_boot[:, j]); z = β̂ / Bootstrap_SE; CI normal-based.
  - **docvis_se block**: bootstrap of se(β). Observed = original OIM SE
    (from `GLM.vcov`); Bootstrap std. err. = std(se_boot[:, j]); z, p, CI
    similarly.

The "depvar_se" naming convention matches Stata's auto-generated equation
labels for `bootstrap _b _se`.
"""
function poisson_boot_b_se_stata(df, formula; B::Int=400, seed::Int=10101,
                                 level::Float64=0.95, quiet::Bool=false,
                                 vce::Symbol=:oim)
    # `vce` controls which SE is bootstrapped on each resample:
    #   :oim    — GLM's default observed-information SE (Stata `poisson`)
    #   :robust — sandwich (n/(n-1)·A⁻¹BA⁻¹) SE   (Stata `poisson, vce(robust)`)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    m   = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β̂   = GLM.coef(m); cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n   = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m)); k = length(β̂)

    function _se_of(model)
        if vce == :robust
            yv  = Float64.(GLM.response(model))
            μ   = GLM.predict(model)
            Xm  = GLM.modelmatrix(model)
            n_b = size(Xm, 1)
            H   = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
            S   = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal((yv .- μ).^2) * Xm
            Hi  = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
            V_  = Hi * S * Hi * (n_b / (n_b - 1))
            return sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_))
        else
            return sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(Matrix(GLM.vcov(model))))
        end
    end
    se_obs = _se_of(m)

    # Each resample returns vcat(β̂_b, se_b) — 2k values per replicate
    bs = obs_bootstrap(dfc; B = B, seed = seed, verbose = false) do d
        m_b = GLM.glm(formula, d, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
        vcat(GLM.coef(m_b), _se_of(m_b))
    end                                              # B × 2k
    β_boot   = bs[:, 1:k]
    se_boot  = bs[:, (k + 1):(2k)]
    boot_se_β  = vec(Statistics.std(β_boot,  dims = 1))
    boot_se_se = vec(Statistics.std(se_boot, dims = 1))

    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1 - level)/2)
    function _z_p_ci(obs_v, boot_se_v)
        z   = obs_v ./ boot_se_v
        p   = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
        lo  = obs_v .- crit .* boot_se_v
        hi  = obs_v .+ crit .* boot_se_v
        return z, p, lo, hi
    end
    z_β,  p_β,  lo_β,  hi_β  = _z_p_ci(β̂,    boot_se_β)
    z_se, p_se, lo_se, hi_se = _z_p_ci(se_obs, boot_se_se)

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        sig_use = sig
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-59s%-13s = %3d\n",
                       "Bootstrap results", "Number of obs", n)
        Printf.@printf("%59s%-13s = %3d\n", "", "Replications", B)
        println()

        # Header
        println("-"^78)
        println("             |   Observed   Bootstrap                         ",
                "Normal-based")
        println("             | coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     ",
                "[", round(Int, 100*level), "% conf. interval]")
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        depvar = string(formula.lhs)
        intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
        slope_idx     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])

        # Block 1: bootstrap of β (equation = depvar)
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", depvar)
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β̂[i]; w=10), g9(boot_se_β[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_β[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_β[i]),
                           g9(lo_β[i]; w=9), g9(hi_β[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # Block 2: bootstrap of se(β) (equation = depvar_se)
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", depvar * "_se")
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(se_obs[i]; w=10), g9(boot_se_se[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_se[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_se[i]),
                           g9(lo_se[i]; w=9), g9(hi_se[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    return (; β = β̂, se_obs, boot_se_β, boot_se_se,
              β_boot, se_boot, model = m, n, B)
end

"""
    panel_bootstrap(f, df, idvar; B=400, seed=10101)

Cluster bootstrap on the panel identifier `idvar`. Applies the user-supplied
function `f(df_resampled)` on each resample and returns a matrix `B × k` of
the vectors `f` returns (one row per replicate).

Useful for computing `vce(boot, reps(B) seed(s))`-style SEs for any estimator.
"""
function panel_bootstrap(f::Function, df, idvar::Symbol; B::Int=400, seed::Int=10101,
                         verbose::Bool=true)
    rng = Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
    ids = unique(df[!, idvar])
    # Pre-index rows by id for faster resampling (avoids O(B*N*n) filtering)
    id_to_rows = Dict{Any, Vector{Int}}()
    for (i, id) in enumerate(df[!, idvar])
        push!(get!(id_to_rows, id, Int[]), i)
    end
    results = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
    n_fail = 0
    for b in 1:B
        boot_ids = StatsBase.sample(rng, ids, length(ids); replace=true)
        # Each sampled cluster gets a fresh unique id so duplicates are not
        # merged by panel estimators. This matches Stata's `bootstrap, cluster()`.
        row_idx = Int[]
        new_id  = Int[]
        for (k, i) in enumerate(boot_ids)
            rows = id_to_rows[i]
            append!(row_idx, rows)
            append!(new_id, fill(k, length(rows)))
        end
        sub = df[row_idx, :]
        sub[!, idvar] = new_id
        try
            push!(results, f(sub))
        catch
            n_fail += 1
        end
    end
    if verbose && n_fail > 0
        @warn "Bootstrap: $n_fail/$B resamples failed (skipped)."
    end
    isempty(results) && error("All bootstrap resamples failed.")
    return reduce(hcat, results)'   # B × k matrix
end

"""
    obs_bootstrap(f, df; B=400, seed=10101, verbose=true)

Observation-level bootstrap — resamples n rows with replacement (no cluster
structure). Matches Stata's `vce(bootstrap)` when no cluster is specified.
"""
function obs_bootstrap(f::Function, df; B::Int=400, seed::Int=10101, verbose::Bool=true)
    rng = Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
    n = nrow(df)
    results = Vector{Vector{Float64}}()
    n_fail = 0
    for b in 1:B
        row_idx = StatsBase.sample(rng, 1:n, n; replace=true)
        sub = df[row_idx, :]
        try
            push!(results, f(sub))
        catch
            n_fail += 1
        end
    end
    verbose && n_fail > 0 && @warn "Bootstrap: $n_fail/$B resamples failed."
    isempty(results) && error("All bootstrap resamples failed.")
    return reduce(hcat, results)'
end

"""
    bsample_stata(df; n=nrow(df), seed=nothing) -> DataFrame

Stata's `bsample` — observation-level resample with replacement. Returns
a new DataFrame with `n` rows drawn from `df` (default `n = nrow(df)`).
Pass `seed` for reproducibility; otherwise uses the global RNG.

Note: Julia's `MersenneTwister` differs from Stata's MT64 RNG, so a fixed
seed will NOT reproduce Stata's exact bootstrap sample.
"""
function bsample_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame;
                       n::Int = DataFrames.nrow(df),
                       seed::Union{Int, Nothing} = nothing)
    rng = seed === nothing ? Random.default_rng() : Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
    idx = StatsBase.sample(rng, 1:DataFrames.nrow(df), n; replace = true)
    return df[idx, :]
end

"""
    bootparametric_nb_stata(df, muhat, α, formula; seed=nothing, quiet=false)

Stata-style parametric NB2 bootstrap (§13.7.2). Generates one resample
from the NB Poisson–gamma mixture using the original-data μ̂ and α:

    ν_i  ~ Gamma(shape = 1/α, scale = α)         (so E[ν] = 1)
    y*_i ~ Poisson(μ̂_i · ν_i)

then fits NB2 of `y*` on the regressors. The depvar in `formula` (e.g.
`dvhat ~ chronic`) is **overwritten** in a copy of `df` with the new
y* draw; all other columns are kept as-is. Mirrors:

    capture drop nu dvhat
    generate nu = rgamma(1/\$alpha, \$alpha)
    generate dvhat = rpoisson(muhat*nu)
    nbreg dvhat chronic

Returns the `nbreg_stata` named tuple. Pass `quiet=true` inside a Monte
Carlo loop to suppress the per-rep table.

Note: Julia's MersenneTwister differs from Stata's MT64, so a fixed seed
will NOT reproduce Stata's exact draw.
"""
function bootparametric_nb_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame,
                                 muhat::AbstractVector, α::Real, formula;
                                 seed::Union{Int, Nothing} = nothing,
                                 quiet::Bool = false)
    rng = seed === nothing ? Random.default_rng() : Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
    n   = length(muhat)
    ν      = Distributions.rand(rng, Distributions.Gamma(1/α, α), n)
    y_star = [Distributions.rand(rng, Distributions.Poisson(m * v))
              for (m, v) in zip(muhat, ν)]
    df_b = DataFrames.DataFrame(df)  # column-wise copy
    df_b[!, Symbol(formula.lhs)] = y_star
    return nbreg_stata(df_b, formula; quiet = quiet)
end

"""
    bootresidual_ols_stata(df, formula; seed=nothing, vcov=nothing,
                           quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style residual bootstrap for OLS with iid errors (§13.7.3). Fits
the original-data regression to get β̂ and residuals û_i, draws
û*_i = û_{idx_i} (resample with replacement), forms y*_i = x_iᵀβ̂ + û*_i,
and refits OLS of y* on the same regressors. Mirrors Stata's
`bootresidual` program, which runs **two** `regress` calls:

    regress docvis chronic         <-- original-data fit (table 1)
    predict xb
    generate ystar = xb + uhat*
    regress ystar chronic          <-- bootstrap fit (table 2)

Unless `quiet=true`, prints both `regress` tables and the
`(option xb assumed; fitted values)` notice that Stata emits between
them. Returns `(; orig, boot, uhat, idx, ystar)` — `orig`/`boot` are
`FixedEffectModels.reg` fits.

Note: Julia's MersenneTwister differs from Stata's MT64, so a fixed
seed will NOT reproduce Stata's exact draw.
"""
function bootresidual_ols_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, formula;
                                seed::Union{Int, Nothing} = nothing,
                                vcov = nothing, quiet::Bool = false)
    rng = seed === nothing ? Random.default_rng() : Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
    m0  = vcov === nothing ?
          FixedEffectModels.reg(df, formula) :
          FixedEffectModels.reg(df, formula, vcov)
    quiet || regress_stata(m0)
    quiet || println("(option xb assumed; fitted values)")

    yvar = Symbol(formula.lhs)
    yhat = FixedEffectModels.predict(m0, df)
    uhat = df[!, yvar] .- yhat
    n    = length(uhat)
    idx  = StatsBase.sample(rng, 1:n, n; replace = true)
    ystar = yhat .+ uhat[idx]
    df_b = DataFrames.DataFrame(df)
    df_b[!, yvar] = ystar
    m_b  = vcov === nothing ?
           FixedEffectModels.reg(df_b, formula) :
           FixedEffectModels.reg(df_b, formula, vcov)
    quiet || regress_stata(m_b)
    return (; orig = m0, boot = m_b, uhat, idx, ystar)
end

"""
    bootwild_ols_stata(df, formula; seed=nothing, vcov=nothing, quiet=false)
    -> NamedTuple

Stata-style wild bootstrap for OLS with iid errors (§13.7.4) using
Mammen's two-point weights:

    P(η = -(√5-1)/2) ≈ 0.7236      (η ≈ -0.618034)
    P(η = +(√5+1)/2) ≈ 0.2764      (η ≈ +1.618034)

Pipeline:
  1. Fit OLS on the original data (table 1).
  2. Compute û = y − x'β̂, draw η_i ∈ {a, b}, form
       û*_i = η_i · û_i,   y*_i = x_iᵀβ̂ + û*_i
  3. Refit OLS of y* on the same regressors (table 2).

Mirrors:

    regress docvis chronic
    predict xb
    predict u, resid
    gen ustar = -0.618034*u
    replace ustar = 1.618034*u if runiform() > 0.723607
    gen ystar = xb + ustar
    regress ystar chronic

Unless `quiet=true`, prints both `regress` tables, the
`(option xb assumed; fitted values)` notice, and the Stata
`(<n> real changes made)` line counting how many η's flipped to b.
Returns `(; orig, boot, η, ustar, ystar)`.

Note: Julia's MersenneTwister differs from Stata's MT64, so a fixed
seed will NOT reproduce Stata's exact draw.
"""
function bootwild_ols_stata(df::DataFrames.AbstractDataFrame, formula;
                            seed::Union{Int, Nothing} = nothing,
                            vcov = nothing, quiet::Bool = false)
    rng = seed === nothing ? Random.default_rng() : Random.MersenneTwister(seed)
    m0  = vcov === nothing ?
          FixedEffectModels.reg(df, formula) :
          FixedEffectModels.reg(df, formula, vcov)
    quiet || regress_stata(m0)
    quiet || println("(option xb assumed; fitted values)")

    yvar = Symbol(formula.lhs)
    yhat = FixedEffectModels.predict(m0, df)
    uhat = df[!, yvar] .- yhat
    n_   = length(uhat)

    a, b      = -0.618034, 1.618034
    flip      = [Random.rand(rng) > 0.723607 for _ in 1:n_]
    η         = ifelse.(flip, b, a)
    ustar     = η .* uhat
    ystar     = yhat .+ ustar
    quiet || println("($(sum(flip)) real changes made)")

    df_b = DataFrames.DataFrame(df)
    df_b[!, yvar] = ystar
    m_b = vcov === nothing ?
          FixedEffectModels.reg(df_b, formula) :
          FixedEffectModels.reg(df_b, formula, vcov)
    quiet || regress_stata(m_b)
    return (; orig = m0, boot = m_b, η, ustar, ystar)
end

"""
    bootstrap_b_table_stata(β_obs, β_boot, coefnames;
                            n_obs, depvar="", level=0.95)

Stata-style `bootstrap _b: <command>` output. Prints the standard table:

  - Header: Number of obs / Replications
  - Coefficient table: "Observed coefficient | Bootstrap std. err. | z | P>|z| |
    Normal-based [CI]" subheaders, one row per coefname

Inputs:
  - `β_obs`     — full-sample observed coefficients (vector, length k)
  - `β_boot`    — bootstrap matrix (B × k)
  - `coefnames` — vector of String labels in the same order as β_obs.
    Use "_cons" for the intercept (Stata convention).
  - `n_obs`     — observation count (printed in the header)
  - `depvar`    — equation label (defaults to blank; Stata uses the depvar)
  - `level`     — confidence level (default 0.95 → 95% CI)

The table is **flat** (single block, no equation banner). For two-block
output (e.g. `bootstrap _b _se`), use the dedicated `poisson_boot_b_se_stata`.
"""
function bootstrap_b_table_stata(β_obs::AbstractVector, β_boot::AbstractMatrix,
                                 coefnames::AbstractVector;
                                 n_obs::Int, depvar::AbstractString = "",
                                 level::Float64 = 0.95,
                                 command::AbstractString = "",
                                 expressions::AbstractVector = String[])
    B    = size(β_boot, 1)
    se_b = vec(Statistics.std(β_boot, dims = 1))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    z    = β_obs ./ se_b
    pv   = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    lo   = β_obs .- crit .* se_b
    hi   = β_obs .+ crit .* se_b

    g9 = function(x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        sig_use = sig
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w_)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    println()
    Printf.@printf("%-59s%-13s = %3s\n",
                   "Bootstrap results", "Number of obs", commafmt(n_obs))
    Printf.@printf("%59s%-13s = %3s\n", "", "Replications", commafmt(B))
    # Optional Stata sub-header for `bootstrap <expr>=...: <command>` form.
    # `command` prints as "Command: <command>"; each `expressions` entry is
    # a `name => formula` String pair, printed as "<name>: <formula>".
    if !isempty(command) || !isempty(expressions)
        println()
        if !isempty(command)
            Printf.@printf("%14s%s\n", "Command:  ", command)
        end
        for ex in expressions
            Printf.@printf("%14s%s\n", "$(ex.first):  ", ex.second)
        end
    end
    println()

    println("-"^78)
    println("             |   Observed   Bootstrap                         Normal-based")
    Printf.@printf("%12s | coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                   depvar, 100*level)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
    for (i, lab) in enumerate(coefnames)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       lab, g9(β_obs[i]; w_=10), g9(se_b[i]; w_=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", pv[i]),
                       g9(lo[i]; w_=9), g9(hi[i]; w_=10))
    end
    println("-"^78)
    return (; β = β_obs, se = se_b, z, p = pv, ci_lo = lo, ci_hi = hi, B, n_obs)
end

"""
    bootstrap_tstar_stata(df, formula, var; B=999, seed=10101, vce=:robust,
                          command="", save_csv=nothing, quiet=false)

Stata-style percentile-t bootstrap for a single Poisson coefficient.
Mirrors:

    quietly poisson <formula>, vce(<vce>)
    local theta = _b[var]
    bootstrap tstar=((_b[var] − `theta')/_se[var]), reps(B) seed(s) … :
        poisson <formula>, vce(<vce>)

Pipeline:
  1. Fit `poisson_stata(df, formula; vce, quiet=true)` on the full sample
     to get the centering θ = β̂_var and σ_θ = SE(β̂_var).
  2. Run `obs_bootstrap(df; B, seed)`, refitting on each resample and
     computing `t* = (β̂*_var − θ) / SE*_var`.
  3. Optionally write the B replicates to `save_csv` (Stata's
     `saving(<file>, replace)` analogue).
  4. Print Stata's bootstrap table via `bootstrap_b_table_stata` with
     "Command:"/"tstar:" sub-header (suppress with `quiet=true`).

Returns `(; β_orig, se_orig, tstars, B, n)` so downstream chunks (e.g. the
percentile-t CI) can read off the original estimates and the t* draws.
"""
function bootstrap_tstar_stata(df, formula, var::Symbol;
                               B::Int=999, seed::Int=10101,
                               vce::Symbol=:robust,
                               command::AbstractString="",
                               save_csv=nothing,
                               quiet::Bool=false)
    fit0 = poisson_stata(df, formula; vce = vce, quiet = true)
    cn0  = fit0.coefnames_glm
    i0   = findfirst(==(string(var)), cn0)
    i0 === nothing && error("'$(var)' not in coefnames=$(cn0)")
    β_orig  = fit0.β_glm[i0]
    se_orig = sqrt(fit0.V_glm[i0, i0])

    tstar_mat = obs_bootstrap(df; B = B, seed = seed, verbose = false) do d
        fit_b = poisson_stata(d, formula; vce = vce, quiet = true)
        cn_b  = fit_b.coefnames_glm
        i_b   = findfirst(==(string(var)), cn_b)
        i_b === nothing && error("'$(var)' not in resample coefnames")
        β_b   = fit_b.β_glm[i_b]
        se_b  = sqrt(fit_b.V_glm[i_b, i_b])
        return [(β_b - β_orig) / se_b]
    end
    tstars = vec(tstar_mat)

    if save_csv !== nothing
        mkpath(dirname(save_csv))
        CSV.write(save_csv, DataFrames.DataFrame(tstar = tstars))
    end

    if !quiet
        bootstrap_b_table_stata([0.0], reshape(tstars, :, 1), ["tstar"];
            n_obs = DataFrames.nrow(df), depvar = "",
            command = command,
            expressions = ["tstar" =>
                "(_b[$(var)]-$(β_orig))/_se[$(var)]"])
    end

    return (; β_orig, se_orig, tstars, B, n = DataFrames.nrow(df))
end

"""
    percentilet_pvalue_stata(tstars, β_orig, se_orig; null=0.0, quiet=false)

Stata-style two-sided symmetric Wald test using a percentile-t bootstrap
distribution:

    p = (1/B) · Σ_b 1{|t*_b| > |t_obs|},   t_obs = (β_orig − null) / se_orig

`tstars` is the bootstrap distribution of `t* = (β̂*_var − θ)/SE*_var`
(the centered version, where θ = β_orig). Mirrors the Stata snippet:

    use percentilet, clear
    quietly count if abs(theta/setheta) < abs(tstar)
    display "p-value = " r(N)/_N

Returns `(; t_obs, p_value, B)`. Prints `p-value = <value>` unless `quiet=true`.
"""
function percentilet_pvalue_stata(tstars::AbstractVector,
                                  β_orig::Real, se_orig::Real;
                                  null::Real = 0.0, quiet::Bool = false)
    t_obs = (β_orig - null) / se_orig
    B     = length(tstars)
    n_ext = sum(abs(t) > abs(t_obs) for t in tstars)
    p_val = n_ext / B
    quiet || @printf("p-value = %.7g\n", p_val)
    return (; t_obs, p_value = p_val, B)
end

"""
    percentilet_ci_stata(tstars, β_orig, se_orig; level=0.95, quiet=false)

Stata-style percentile-t bootstrap confidence interval for a parameter θ
(estimated by `β_orig`, with original full-sample SE `se_orig`) given the
bootstrap distribution `tstars` of `t* = (β̂*−θ)/SE*`:

    q_lo = quantile(tstars, α/2),    q_hi = quantile(tstars, 1−α/2)
    [lb, ub] = [θ + q_lo·SE_θ,   θ + q_hi·SE_θ]

Mirrors the Stata snippet:

    _pctile tstar, p(2.5,97.5)
    scalar lb = `theta' + r(r1)*`setheta'
    scalar ub = `theta' + r(r2)*`setheta'
    display "2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of t* distn: " r(r1) ", " r(r2) _n ///
        "95 percent percentile-t confidence interval is  (" lb ","  ub ")"

Returns `(; q_lo, q_hi, lb, ub, level)`. Prints the two-line Stata display
unless `quiet=true`.
"""
function percentilet_ci_stata(tstars::AbstractVector,
                              β_orig::Real, se_orig::Real;
                              level::Real = 0.95, quiet::Bool = false)
    α    = 1 - level
    plo  = α / 2
    phi  = 1 - α / 2
    q_lo = Statistics.quantile(tstars, plo)
    q_hi = Statistics.quantile(tstars, phi)
    lb   = β_orig + q_lo * se_orig
    ub   = β_orig + q_hi * se_orig

    # Stata `display` default ≈ %~9.0g: 7 sig digits, strip leading 0 for |x|<1.
    function gd(x)
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.7g", x)
        (0 < abs(x) < 1) && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        return s
    end
    pct_str(p) = (q = p * 100; isinteger(q) ? string(Int(q)) :
                  rstrip(rstrip(Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", q), '0'), '.'))

    if !quiet
        @printf("%s and %s percentiles of t* distn: %s, %s\n",
                pct_str(plo), pct_str(phi), gd(q_lo), gd(q_hi))
        @printf("%g percent percentile-t confidence interval is  (%s,%s)\n",
                level * 100, gd(lb), gd(ub))
    end
    return (; q_lo, q_hi, lb, ub, level)
end

"""
    mybootstrap_stata(df, formula, var; B=999, seed=10101, vce=:robust,
                      command="", null=0.0, quiet=false)

One-shot percentile-t bootstrap p-value (Stata's `mybootstrap` program in
§13.6.3): fits the original full-sample model, runs `B` observation-level
bootstrap replications building the centered t* distribution
`t*_b = (β̂*_var − β_orig) / SE*_var`, and returns the symmetric two-sided
p-value  `(1/B)·Σ 1{|t*_b| > |t_obs|}`,  `t_obs = (β_orig − null)/SE_orig`.

Thin wrapper over `bootstrap_tstar_stata` + `percentilet_pvalue_stata`.
Suitable for embedding in a Monte-Carlo loop that runs the whole bootstrap
many times with different seeds.

Returns `(; pvalue, t_obs, B, tstars, β_orig, se_orig)`. Prints
`p-value = <value>` unless `quiet=true`.
"""
function mybootstrap_stata(df, formula, var::Symbol;
                           B::Int=999, seed::Int=10101,
                           vce::Symbol=:robust,
                           command::AbstractString="",
                           null::Real=0.0, quiet::Bool=false)
    res = bootstrap_tstar_stata(df, formula, var;
                                B=B, seed=seed, vce=vce,
                                command=command, quiet=true)
    pv  = percentilet_pvalue_stata(res.tstars, res.β_orig, res.se_orig;
                                   null=null, quiet=quiet)
    return (; pvalue = pv.p_value, t_obs = pv.t_obs, B = pv.B,
              tstars = res.tstars, β_orig = res.β_orig, se_orig = res.se_orig)
end

function poisson_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:robust, level::Float64=0.95,
                       quiet::Bool=false,
                       layout::Union{Nothing,AbstractVector}=nothing,
                       header_style::Symbol=:poisson,
                       cluster_var=nothing)
    # Drop missing for variables in formula (and the cluster var, if any)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    cols   = cluster_var === nothing ? needed :
                                       vcat(needed, [Symbol(cluster_var)])
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end

    # Fit Poisson GLM
    m = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β  = GLM.coef(m)
    cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m))
    yv = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
    μ  = GLM.predict(m)
    Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)
    k  = size(Xm, 2)

    # If `cluster_var` is given, force vce → :cluster regardless of caller's
    # choice (Stata's `vce(cluster <var>)` syntax), and capture cluster count.
    n_clusters = 0
    if cluster_var !== nothing
        vce = :cluster
        n_clusters = length(unique(dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]))
    end

    # SE: robust sandwich (default) / cluster-robust (CR1) / OIM.
    # Stata's `vce(robust)` uses n/(n-1) finite-sample correction.
    # `vce(cluster G)` uses (G/(G-1))·(n-1)/(n-k) and aggregates scores by
    # cluster: B = Σ_g (X_g'(y_g − μ_g)) (X_g'(y_g − μ_g))'.
    if vce == :robust
        H = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
        meat = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal((yv .- μ).^2) * Xm
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
        V = Hinv * meat * Hinv * (n / (n - 1))
    elseif vce == :cluster
        cluster_var === nothing &&
            error("vce = :cluster requires `cluster_var = :varname`")
        cl = dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]
        u  = (yv .- μ) .* Xm                # n×k per-obs scores X_i·(y_i−μ_i)
        # Aggregate scores by cluster, then meat = Σ_g s_g s_g'.
        meat = zeros(k, k)
        for g in unique(cl)
            sg = vec(sum(u[cl .== g, :], dims = 1))
            meat .+= sg * sg'
        end
        H    = Xm' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(μ) * Xm
        Hinv = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.cholesky(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H)))
        G    = n_clusters
        # Stata's `poisson, vce(cluster)` uses ONLY the G/(G−1) cluster
        # adjustment — no extra (n−1)/(n−k) factor (that one is OLS-style).
        V    = Hinv * meat * Hinv * (G / (G - 1))
    else
        V = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    # Slopes (excluding intercept) — used for both Wald and LR
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:length(β), [intercept_idx])
    Wald = NaN; Wald_p = NaN
    if !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_slope = β[slope_idx]
        V_slope = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald = β_slope' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_slope) * β_slope
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), Wald)
    end

    # Log pseudolikelihood and Pseudo R² (McFadden's-like: 1 - LL/LL_null)
    ll  = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    # Null model: intercept only
    m_null = GLM.glm(StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1),
                     dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    ll_null = GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null

    # LR chi² on slopes — Stata's default `poisson` reports `LR chi2(k)`;
    # `vce(robust|cluster)` switches it to `Wald chi2(k)` (LR is invalid
    # under misspecification of the likelihood).
    LR_chi2 = !isempty(slope_idx) ? 2 * (ll - ll_null) : NaN
    LR_p    = !isempty(slope_idx) ?
              1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), LR_chi2) :
              NaN

    # Stata %9.0g formatter — sign-aware width cap (cap=9 except cap=10 for
    # negative |x|<1, where leading-zero strip saves a char). Without this
    # asymmetry, negative |x|<1 values would lose a digit vs Stata's output.
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        if 0 < abs(x) < 1
            s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
        end
        return lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(num)
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1
            push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3
        end
        return (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # Skip the entire Stata-style printout when quiet=true (mirrors Stata's
    # `quietly poisson ...`). Useful for chapter chunks that just need β/V/X
    # for downstream margins/dydx/etc. and don't want to repeat the table.
    if !quiet
    # Print Stata-style header. Two layouts:
    #   :poisson — Stata's `poisson` command output. Top-left says "Poisson
    #              regression", and the right column lists Number of obs /
    #              Wald chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Pseudo R2 over four lines,
    #              with "Log pseudolikelihood = …" on the last line at left.
    #   :ml      — Stata's `ml maximize` output. No "Poisson regression"
    #              header; the right column lists Number of obs / Wald
    #              chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 over three lines, with "Log
    #              [pseudo]likelihood = …" on the third line at left, and
    #              no Pseudo R2 row.
    println()
    if header_style == :ml
        # Stata `ml maximize` right-block format: 13-char left-padded label,
        # " = ", then a value field whose width is the max of the three
        # value strings plus 1 (so the longest value sits 1 space after `=`,
        # shorter ones are right-aligned). The whole right block is positioned
        # flush right at col 78 by adjusting the leading whitespace.
        nstr = commafmt(n)
        wstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", Wald) : ""
        pstr = isfinite(Wald) ? Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", Wald_p) : ""
        vw   = maximum(length, (nstr, wstr, pstr))
        rblock = 13 + 3 + vw
        lead   = max(0, 78 - rblock)
        ws     = " " ^ lead
        println(ws, rpad("Number of obs", 13), " = ", lpad(nstr, vw))
        if isfinite(Wald)
            println(ws, rpad("Wald chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", 13),
                    " = ", lpad(wstr, vw))
        end
        ll_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str   = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.3f", ll_label, ll)
        println(rpad(ll_str, lead), rpad("Prob > chi2", 13), " = ", lpad(pstr, vw))
    else
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Poisson regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        # `LR chi2` for OIM (default), `Wald chi2` for robust/cluster.
        chi2_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "Wald" : "LR"
        chi2_val   = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? Wald   : LR_chi2
        chi2_p     = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? Wald_p : LR_p
        if isfinite(chi2_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
```
