```{julia}
                           "$chi2_label chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", chi2_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", chi2_p)
        end
        ll_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ?
                   "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.5f", ll_label, ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad_h  = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad_h, r2_str)
    end
    println()

    # Cluster sub-note (Stata: "(Std. err. adjusted for G clusters in <var>)"),
    # right-aligned at col 78.
    if vce == :cluster
        cl_str = Printf.@sprintf("(Std. err. adjusted for %d clusters in %s)",
                                 n_clusters, cluster_var)
        println(lpad(cl_str, 78))
    end

    # Coefficient table. Stata uses lowercase "std. err." under the "Robust"
    # subheader for `vce(robust)` / `vce(cluster …)` and capital "Std. err."
    # for the default OIM.
    println("-"^78)
    if vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
        println("             |               Robust")
    end
    se_label = (vce == :robust || vce == :cluster) ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
    Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
                   string(formula.lhs), se_label)
    println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

    # `_print_row(label, idx)` renders a single row in Stata's standard
    # 7-column layout. `_lookup(key)` finds the GLM-order index from a
    # coefname or returns the index directly.
    _print_row(label, idx) = Printf.@printf(
        "%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
        label, g9(β[idx]; w=10), g9(se[idx]; w=9),
        Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[idx]),
        Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[idx]),
        g9(ci_lo[idx]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[idx]; w=10))
    _lookup(key) = key isa Integer ? Int(key) :
        (let i = findfirst(==(string(key)), cn)
            i === nothing && error("'$(key)' not found in coefnames=$(cn)")
            i
        end)

    if layout === nothing
        # Default layout: slopes (in formula order) first, then _cons.
        for i in slope_idx
            _print_row(cn[i], i)
        end
        intercept_idx !== nothing && _print_row("_cons", intercept_idx)
    else
        # Custom layout. Each entry is one of:
        #   :blank                       → empty separator row "             |"
        #   String  => key                → simple row, label = String
        #   Vector{String} => key         → multi-line interaction block: all
        #                                    but the last element are header
        #                                    lines (printed as `<line>|`),
        #                                    last element is the row label.
        # `key` can be a coefname (matched against the GLM-order coefnames)
        # or a 1-based integer index into β.
        for entry in layout
            if entry === :blank
                println("             |")
            elseif entry isa Pair
                lab, key = entry.first, entry.second
                # `label => :omitted` — Stata-style "(omitted)" row for a
                # variable that was dropped due to collinearity. Prints
                # "        label |          0  (omitted)" with no key lookup.
                if key === :omitted
                    Printf.@printf("%12s |          0  (omitted)\n", string(lab))
                    continue
                end
                idx = _lookup(key)
                if lab isa AbstractVector
                    for h in lab[1:end-1]
                        println(h, "|")
                    end
                    _print_row(string(lab[end]), idx)
                else
                    _print_row(string(lab), idx)
                end
            else
                error("Unsupported layout entry: $entry (use :blank or label=>key)")
            end
        end
    end
    println("-"^78)
    end  # if !quiet

    # Return values in *Stata's display order*: slopes first, then _cons.
    # That way the margins / nlcom / lincom / dydx helpers can be called
    # directly on these without any reordering, and the constant always
    # sits at the end of β (matching the convention used throughout the
    # downstream chapter chunks).
    if intercept_idx === nothing
        ord = collect(slope_idx)
        cn_ord = cn[ord]
    else
        ord = vcat(collect(slope_idx), [intercept_idx])
        cn_ord = vcat(cn[slope_idx], "_cons")
    end
    β_ord  = β[ord]
    se_ord = se[ord]
    V_ord  = V[ord, ord]
    X_ord  = Xm[:, ord]   # last column = ones (the constant)

    return (; model=m, df=dfc, formula,
              β=β_ord, se=se_ord, V=V_ord, X=X_ord,
              coefnames=cn_ord,
              Wald, Wald_p, ll, pseudo_r2, n, k,
              # Originals (GLM order) preserved for any code that needs them:
              β_glm=β, V_glm=V, X_glm=Xm, coefnames_glm=cn)
end

"""
    poisson_jackknife_stata(df, formula; mse=true, level=0.95, quiet=false)
        -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `poisson <formula>, vce(jackknife[, mse nodots])`. Delete-1
jackknife SE for the Poisson coefficients:

    For each i = 1..n,  β̂_(i) = MLE on df without observation i

    V_jack = (n-1)/n · Σ_i (β̂_(i) − c)(β̂_(i) − c)ᵀ
        c = β̂  (full-sample MLE)   if `mse = true`   (Stata `mse` option)
        c = β̄  (mean of β̂_(i))    otherwise         (Stata default)

Inference uses a t-distribution with df = n − 1; the omnibus statistic
is `F(k_slopes, n − 1) = (β'V⁻¹β) / k_slopes`. Prints the Stata-format
header (Number of obs / Replications / F / Prob > F / Log likelihood /
Pseudo R²), the `Jackknife` sub-banner, and the coefficient table.

Returns `(; β, V, se, t, p, ci_lo, ci_hi, β_jack, n, k, coefnames,
F, F_p, ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, model)`. β-vector and table rows are in
Stata-display order (slopes first, `_cons` last).
"""
function poisson_jackknife_stata(df, formula; mse::Bool = true,
                                 level::Float64 = 0.95,
                                 quiet::Bool = false)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end

    # Full-sample fit (OIM for β̂, ll; jackknife replaces V).
    fit  = poisson_stata(dfc, formula; vce = :oim, quiet = true)
    β_glm  = fit.β_glm
    cn     = fit.coefnames_glm
    n      = fit.n
    k      = fit.k
    ll     = fit.ll
    ll_null = ll / (1 - fit.pseudo_r2)
    pseudo_r2 = fit.pseudo_r2

    # Leave-one-out fits.
    β_jack = Matrix{Float64}(undef, n, k)
    rows = 1:DataFrames.nrow(dfc)
    for i in 1:n
        fit_i = poisson_stata(dfc[setdiff(rows, i), :], formula;
                              vce = :oim, quiet = true)
        # Match coefnames order to the original full-sample fit.
        β_jack[i, :] = [fit_i.β_glm[findfirst(==(name), fit_i.coefnames_glm)]
                        for name in cn]
    end

    # Jackknife vcov.
    centre = mse ? β_glm : vec(Statistics.mean(β_jack, dims = 1))
    devs   = β_jack .- centre'
    V_jack = ((n - 1) / n) * (devs' * devs)

    # Inference (t with df = n − 1).
    se   = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_jack))
    t    = β_glm ./ se
    df_t = n - 1
    p    = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.TDist(df_t), abs.(t)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.TDist(df_t), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β_glm .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β_glm .+ crit .* se

    # F-test on slopes.
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    F_val, F_p = NaN, NaN
    if !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_s = β_glm[slope_idx]
        V_s = V_jack[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald_s = β_s' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_s) * β_s
        F_val  = Wald_s / length(slope_idx)
        F_p    = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.FDist(length(slope_idx), df_t), F_val)
    end

    # Stata `%9.0g` formatter (sign-aware width cap; same as poisson_stata).
    function g9(x; w::Int = 10, sig::Int = 7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(num)
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Poisson regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6s\n", "", "Replications", commafmt(n))
        if isfinite(F_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                           "F($(length(slope_idx)), $df_t)", F_val)
            Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > F", F_p)
        end
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("Log likelihood = %.5f", ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad_h  = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad_h, r2_str)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        println("             |              Jackknife")
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  std. err.       t    P>|t|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(collect(slope_idx), [intercept_idx])
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β_glm[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", t[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    # Stata-display order (slopes first, _cons last) for downstream helpers.
    ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                      vcat(collect(slope_idx), [intercept_idx])
    cn_ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? cn[ord] : vcat(cn[slope_idx], "_cons")
    return (; β = β_glm[ord], V = V_jack[ord, ord], se = se[ord],
              t = t[ord], p = p[ord], ci_lo = ci_lo[ord], ci_hi = ci_hi[ord],
              β_jack, coefnames = cn_ord, n, k, F = F_val, F_p,
              ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, model = fit.model)
end

"""
    probit_stata(df, formula; vce=:oim, level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `probit <depvar> <regs> [, vce(robust)]`. Fits a Binomial GLM
with `ProbitLink` and prints Stata's exact `probit` output:

  - Header: Number of obs / LR chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 / Log likelihood / Pseudo R²
    (NB: `LR chi2`, NOT `Wald chi2` — Stata uses 2·(ll − ll_null) for the
    overall fit statistic in `probit` even with `vce(robust)`.)
  - Coefficient table in Stata-display order (slopes first, _cons last).

Returns `(; model, β, se, V, X, coefnames, ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, n, k,
          β_glm, V_glm, X_glm, coefnames_glm)` so downstream code (e.g.
Heckman two-step) can reuse the fitted probit linear index.
"""
function probit_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:oim, level::Float64=0.95,
                      quiet::Bool=false)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end
    # Drop any rows with non-finite values (NaN/Inf in computed columns
    # like `linc = log(hhincome)` would crash GLM.jl's IRLS at the
    # `isfinite(dev)` assertion). `dropmissing` only handles `Missing`.
    keep = trues(DataFrames.nrow(dfc))
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        eltype(col) <: Real || continue
        for i in eachindex(col)
            keep[i] &= isfinite(col[i])
        end
    end
    dfc = dfc[keep, :]
    # Fit probit. Default IRLS sometimes fails its `isfinite(dev)` assertion
    # when the design matrix has wide-range columns (e.g. `age2`); in that
    # case we warm-start from a logit fit's β rescaled by ≈1/1.81 (the
    # asymptotic logit→probit coefficient ratio sqrt(π/3)).
    m = try
        GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    catch err
        if err isa AssertionError && occursin("isfinite", string(err))
            m_logit = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.LogitLink())
            β_init  = GLM.coef(m_logit) ./ 1.81
            GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink();
                    start = β_init)
        else
            rethrow(err)
        end
    end
    β  = GLM.coef(m); cn = GLM.coefnames(m)
    n  = Int(StatsBase.nobs(m)); k = length(β)
    yv = Float64.(GLM.response(m))
    Xm = GLM.modelmatrix(m)

    V = if vce == :robust
        # Robust sandwich for probit: V = A · meat · A · (n/(n-1)) with
        # A = OIM vcov and meat = Σ s_i s_iᵀ where the per-obs score is
        # s_i = ((y_i − μ_i) / [μ_i(1−μ_i)]) · φ(η_i) · x_i.
        η  = Xm * β                                 # linear index
        μ  = GLM.predict(m)
        ϕ  = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), η)
        u  = (yv .- μ) ./ (μ .* (1 .- μ)) .* ϕ
        s  = u .* Xm
        meat = s' * s
        A = Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))                     # OIM vcov is A⁻¹ already
        A * meat * A * (n / (n - 1))
    else
        Matrix(GLM.vcov(m))
    end
    se = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    z  = β ./ se
    p_z = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
    crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    ci_lo = β .- crit .* se
    ci_hi = β .+ crit .* se

    ll = GLM.loglikelihood(m)
    m_null = GLM.glm(StatsModels.term(Symbol(formula.lhs)) ~ StatsModels.term(1),
                     dfc, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    ll_null = GLM.loglikelihood(m_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null
    LR = 2 * (ll - ll_null)
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    LR_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)), LR)

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %6s\n",
                       "Probit regression", "Number of obs", commafmt(n))
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.2f\n", "",
                       "LR chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", LR)
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %6.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", LR_p)
        ll_str = Printf.@sprintf("Log likelihood = %.4f", ll)
        r2_str = Printf.@sprintf("%-13s = %6.4f", "Pseudo R2", pseudo_r2)
        pad    = max(0, 78 - length(ll_str) - length(r2_str))
        println(ll_str, " "^pad, r2_str)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β[i]; w=10), g9(se[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_z[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^78)
    end

    intercept_idx2 = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx2     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx2])
    ord2 = intercept_idx2 === nothing ? collect(slope_idx2) :
                                        vcat(slope_idx2, [intercept_idx2])
    cn_ord = intercept_idx2 === nothing ? cn[ord2] :
                                          vcat(cn[slope_idx2], "_cons")
    return (; model = m, β = β[ord2], se = se[ord2], V = V[ord2, ord2],
              X = Xm[:, ord2], coefnames = cn_ord,
              ll, ll_null, pseudo_r2, LR, LR_p, n, k,
              β_glm = β, V_glm = V, X_glm = Xm, coefnames_glm = cn)
end

"""
    heckman_twostep_stata(df, fml_outcome, fml_selection;
                         depvar_y="lny", depvar_d="dy", level=0.95, quiet=false)

Stata-style `heckman <y> <xs>, select(<d> = <zs>) twostep`. Implements the
classic Heckman (1979) two-step estimator with proper variance correction
for the first-stage probit estimation:

  Stage 1: probit(`d ~ zs`) on full sample → γ̂
           λ_i = φ(z_i'γ̂)/Φ(z_i'γ̂)
  Stage 2: OLS(`y ~ xs + λ`) on positive subsample → α̂ = (β̂, β̂_λ)
           σ̂² = (ε̂'ε̂)/n₂ + β̂_λ² · mean(δ_i over positives)
                where δ_i = λ_i · (λ_i + z_i'γ̂)
           ρ̂ = β̂_λ / σ̂   (and Stata's `lambda` output is β̂_λ = ρ̂·σ̂)

The variance of α̂ corrects for stage-1 sampling variability:
  V(α̂) = σ̂² · (X*'X*)⁻¹ · {X*'(I − ρ̂²Δ)X* + ρ̂²·X*'Δ·Z·Vγ·Z'Δ·X*} · (X*'X*)⁻¹
  where X* = [X_pos | λ_pos], Δ = diag(δ_pos), Vγ = (Z'diag(δ_full)Z)⁻¹.

Prints Stata's three-block output (lny / dy / /mills) with the corrected SEs
plus σ̂ and ρ̂. Returns the NamedTuple
`(; β_outcome, β_selection, β_lambda, σ, ρ, V_outcome, n, n_pos, n_zero, …)`.
"""
function heckman_twostep_stata(df, fml_outcome, fml_selection;
                               depvar_y::AbstractString="lny",
                               depvar_d::AbstractString="dy",
                               level::Float64=0.95, quiet::Bool=false)
    # Stage 1 — probit on the FULL sample with non-missing SELECTION vars
    # only. We must NOT dropmissing on outcome vars here, since the outcome
    # variable (e.g. `lny`) is legitimately missing for unselected rows
    # (where y = 0). Including it in the dropmissing would eliminate the
    # unselected rows and make the probit degenerate (all dy = 1).
    sel_vars = StatsModels.termvars(fml_selection)
    out_vars = StatsModels.termvars(fml_outcome)
    needed   = unique(vcat(sel_vars, out_vars))
    # `dropmissing(df, cols)` only requires `cols` to be non-missing while
    # keeping all columns. Outcome `lny` retains its missing values.
    df_h = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, needed], sel_vars)
    n_full = DataFrames.nrow(df_h)

    m_pr = GLM.glm(fml_selection, df_h,
                   Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    γ̂   = GLM.coef(m_pr); cn_pr = GLM.coefnames(m_pr)
    Z   = GLM.modelmatrix(m_pr)
    xb_full = Z * γ̂
    λ_full  = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb_full) ./
              Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb_full)
    δ_full  = λ_full .* (λ_full .+ xb_full)

    # Selection mask. Use plain `Int == 1` rather than `Float64 > 0` because
    # some loaded packages in some sessions type-pirate `>`/comparison
    # broadcasting for Float64. `Int == Int` is essentially impossible to
    # pirate, so this form is robust.
    d_full = Int.(df_h[!, Symbol(depvar_d)])
    is_pos = Bool[d == 1 for d in d_full]
    n_pos  = sum(is_pos); n_zero = n_full - n_pos

    # Stage 2 — OLS on positives, with λ as additional regressor
    df_pos = df_h[is_pos, :]
    df_pos.invmills = λ_full[is_pos]
    fml_ols = StatsModels.term(Symbol(depvar_y)) ~
              sum(StatsModels.term.(out_vars[2:end])) +
              StatsModels.term(:invmills)
    # Build X_pos manually so we control column order
    out_xs = out_vars[2:end]   # skip lhs
    X_pos  = hcat(ones(n_pos),
                 [Float64.(df_pos[!, v]) for v in out_xs]...,
                 df_pos.invmills)
    y_pos  = Float64.(df_pos[!, Symbol(depvar_y)])
    α̂      = X_pos \ y_pos
    ε̂      = y_pos .- X_pos * α̂

    β̂_λ    = α̂[end]
    δ_pos  = δ_full[is_pos]
    σ̂²     = (ε̂'ε̂) / n_pos + β̂_λ^2 * Statistics.mean(δ_pos)
    σ̂      = sqrt(σ̂²)
    ρ̂      = β̂_λ / σ̂

    # Heckman 2-step variance with stage-1 correction. Use the probit
    # Fisher information matrix V(γ̂) = (Σ w_i z_i z_i')⁻¹ with
    # w_i = φ_i² / [Φ_i (1−Φ_i)] — this is what Stata's `heckman` uses for
    # the first-stage VCE, NOT the Heckman-1979 (Z'ΔZ)⁻¹ form (which gives
    # SEs ~0.2% larger because Δ ≠ Fisher info weights).
    safe_sym_inv(A; rtol::Float64=1e-10) = begin
        As = LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(A)
        try
            LinearAlgebra.inv(As)
        catch
            LinearAlgebra.pinv(Matrix(As); rtol=rtol)
        end
    end

    XX_inv = safe_sym_inv(X_pos' * X_pos)
    Φ_full = clamp.(Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb_full), 1e-12, 1 - 1e-12)
    φ_full = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb_full)
    w_full = (φ_full .^ 2) ./ (Φ_full .* (1 .- Φ_full))
    A_γ    = Z' * LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(w_full) * Z       # probit Fisher info
    Vγ     = safe_sym_inv(A_γ)
    Z_pos  = Z[is_pos, :]
    D_pos  = LinearAlgebra.Diagonal(δ_pos)
    M1     = X_pos' * (LinearAlgebra.I(n_pos) - ρ̂^2 .* D_pos) * X_pos
    M2     = ρ̂^2 .* (X_pos' * D_pos * Z_pos) * Vγ * (Z_pos' * D_pos * X_pos)
    V_α    = σ̂² .* XX_inv * (M1 + M2) * XX_inv
    se_α   = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V_α), 0.0))

    # Coefficient names for outcome (cons last, as Stata)
    cn_out = vcat(string.(out_xs), ["_cons"])
    # α̂ order: (Intercept), out_xs..., invmills. Reorder for Stata: out_xs, _cons.
    # Indices in α̂: 1=cons, 2..k+1=xs, k+2=invmills
    k_out  = length(out_xs)
    α̂_disp = vcat(α̂[2:k_out+1], [α̂[1]])
    se_disp = vcat(se_α[2:k_out+1], [se_α[1]])
    α_lam  = α̂[end]; se_lam = se_α[end]

    z_disp = α̂_disp ./ se_disp
    p_disp = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_disp)))
    crit   = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    lo_disp = α̂_disp .- crit .* se_disp
    hi_disp = α̂_disp .+ crit .* se_disp

    z_lam = α_lam / se_lam
    p_lam = 2 * (1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Normal(), abs(z_lam)))
    lo_lam = α_lam - crit * se_lam; hi_lam = α_lam + crit * se_lam

    # Selection equation SEs from probit (no correction needed)
    se_pr = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(Matrix(GLM.vcov(m_pr))))
    z_pr  = γ̂ ./ se_pr
    p_pr  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_pr)))
    lo_pr = γ̂ .- crit .* se_pr; hi_pr = γ̂ .+ crit .* se_pr
    i_int_pr = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn_pr)
    slope_pr = setdiff(1:length(γ̂), [i_int_pr])
    ord_pr   = vcat(slope_pr, [i_int_pr])
    cn_pr_ord = vcat(cn_pr[slope_pr], "_cons")
    γ̂_disp = γ̂[ord_pr]; se_pr_disp = se_pr[ord_pr]
    z_pr_disp = z_pr[ord_pr]; p_pr_disp = p_pr[ord_pr]
    lo_pr_disp = lo_pr[ord_pr]; hi_pr_disp = hi_pr[ord_pr]

    # Wald chi²(k_out) on outcome slopes — uses corrected V
    βs = α̂_disp[1:end-1]   # (without _cons)
    Vs = V_α[2:k_out+1, 2:k_out+1]
    Wald = try
        (βs' * (LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(Vs) \ βs))::Float64
    catch
        (βs' * LinearAlgebra.pinv(Vs) * βs)::Float64
    end
    Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(k_out), Wald)

    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    commafmt(num) = begin
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%-48s%-13s = %10s\n",
                       "Heckman selection model -- two-step estimates",
                       "Number of obs", commafmt(n_full))
        Printf.@printf("%-48s    %-13s = %10s\n",
                       "(regression model with sample selection)",
                       "Selected", commafmt(n_pos))
        Printf.@printf("%-48s    %-13s = %10s\n",
                       "", "Nonselected", commafmt(n_zero))
        println()
        Printf.@printf("%48s%-13s = %10.2f\n", "",
                       "Wald chi2($(k_out))", Wald)
        Printf.@printf("%48s%-13s = %10.4f\n", "", "Prob > chi2", Wald_p)
        println()

        println("-"^78)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       "", 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # lny block
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", depvar_y)
        for i in 1:k_out
            label = string(out_xs[i])
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(α̂_disp[i]; w=10), g9(se_disp[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_disp[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_disp[i]),
                           g9(lo_disp[i]; w=9), g9(hi_disp[i]; w=10))
        end
        # _cons row for outcome
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       "_cons", g9(α̂_disp[end]; w=10), g9(se_disp[end]; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_disp[end]),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_disp[end]),
                       g9(lo_disp[end]; w=9), g9(hi_disp[end]; w=10))
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # dy block
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", depvar_d)
        for i in eachindex(γ̂_disp)
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           cn_pr_ord[i],
                           g9(γ̂_disp[i]; w=10), g9(se_pr_disp[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_pr_disp[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_pr_disp[i]),
                           g9(lo_pr_disp[i]; w=9), g9(hi_pr_disp[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)

        # /mills block
        Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", "/mills")
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                       "lambda",
                       g9(α_lam; w=10), g9(se_lam; w=9),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_lam),
                       Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_lam),
                       g9(lo_lam; w=9), g9(hi_lam; w=10))
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s\n", "rho",   Printf.@sprintf("%9.5f",  ρ̂))
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s\n", "sigma", Printf.@sprintf("%9.7f", σ̂))
        println("-"^78)
    end

    α̂_outcome_dict = Dict(zip(vcat(string.(out_xs), ["_cons"]), α̂_disp))
    return (; β_outcome = α̂_disp, se_outcome = se_disp, V_outcome = V_α,
              β_selection = γ̂, se_selection = se_pr, β_lambda = α_lam,
              se_lambda = se_lam, σ = σ̂, ρ = ρ̂,
              n = n_full, n_pos, n_zero,
              outcome_coefnames = vcat(string.(out_xs), ["_cons"]),
              selection_coefnames = cn_pr_ord)
end

"""
    nbreg_stata(df, formula; vce=:oim, level=0.95, quiet=false) -> NamedTuple

Stata-style `nbreg <depvar> <regs>, [vce(robust)] nolog`. Fits the NB2
model jointly in (β, lnα) by maximising the log-likelihood

    lnf_i = lnΓ(y_i + 1/α) − lnΓ(1/α) − lnΓ(y_i + 1)
            − (y_i + 1/α) · ln(1 + α·μ_i) + y_i·ln(α) + y_i·θ_i,
    θ_i = x_iᵀβ,  μ_i = exp(θ_i)

via `Optim.LBFGS` with autodiff and uses the inverse Hessian as the OIM
vcov. Prints the Stata header (Number of obs / LR chi2(k) / Prob > chi2 /
Pseudo R²) followed by the coefficient table with `/lnalpha` and `alpha`
rows, and finally the LR test of `α = 0` (NB → Poisson) reported as
`chibar2(01)` with the half-mixture p-value `0.5·P(χ²₁ > LR)`.

Returns `(; model, β_glm, V_glm, coefnames_glm, lnα, α, ll, n, k,
LR_alpha, p_chibar)`.
"""
function nbreg_stata(df, formula; vce::Symbol=:oim, level::Float64=0.95,
                    quiet::Bool=false, cluster_var=nothing)
    needed = StatsModels.termvars(formula)
    cols   = cluster_var === nothing ? needed :
                                       vcat(needed, [Symbol(cluster_var)])
    dfc = DataFrames.dropmissing(df[:, cols])
    for c in needed
        col = dfc[!, c]
        if eltype(col) <: Union{Missing, Float32} || eltype(col) === Float32
            dfc[!, c] = Float64.(col)
        end
    end

    # Fit Poisson first: gives β starting values + LL_pois for the LR test
    m_pois  = GLM.glm(formula, dfc, Distributions.Poisson(), GLM.LogLink())
    β0      = GLM.coef(m_pois)
    ll_pois = GLM.loglikelihood(m_pois)
    yv      = Float64.(GLM.response(m_pois))
    Xm      = GLM.modelmatrix(m_pois)
    cn      = GLM.coefnames(m_pois)
    n       = size(Xm, 1)
    k       = size(Xm, 2)

    # NB log-likelihood (parameters are β stacked with lnα — last entry)
    function nb_nll(p)
        β  = p[1:k]; α = exp(p[k + 1])
        η  = Xm * β; μ = exp.(η); inv_α = 1 / α
        ll = sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(yv .+ inv_α) .-
                 SpecialFunctions.loggamma(inv_α) .-
                 SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(yv .+ 1) .-
                 (yv .+ inv_α) .* log.(1 .+ α .* μ) .+
                 yv .* log(α) .+ yv .* η)
        return -ll
    end
    # Use NelderMead (derivative-free) to avoid forwarding ForwardDiff Duals
    # through `SpecialFunctions.gamma_inc`, which lacks Dual methods and
    # produces "no method matching" errors during autodiff. We get a high-
    # quality optimum from LBFGS (warm-started from Poisson β) but refine via
    # NelderMead and use central finite differences for the Hessian.
    p0  = Float64.(vcat(β0, log(1.0)))
    res = _optimize_compat(nb_nll, p0, Optim.NelderMead(),
                         Optim.Options(g_tol     = 1e-10,
                                       x_abstol  = 1e-10,
                                       f_reltol  = 1e-12,
                                       iterations = 5000))
    p̂   = Float64.(Optim.minimizer(res))
    β̂   = p̂[1:k]
    lnα = p̂[k + 1]
    α   = exp(lnα)
    ll  = -nb_nll(p̂)::Float64

    # OIM vcov from inverse Hessian via central finite differences (avoids
    # any autodiff path through gamma_inc / loggamma).
    function _fd_hessian(f::Function, x::AbstractVector{<:Real})
        n_p = length(x)
        H   = zeros(n_p, n_p)
        h   = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(x), 1.0)  # ~1e-4 step
        f0  = f(x)
        for i in 1:n_p
            xpi = copy(x); xmi = copy(x)
            xpi[i] += h[i]; xmi[i] -= h[i]
            fpi, fmi = f(xpi), f(xmi)
            H[i, i] = (fpi - 2*f0 + fmi) / h[i]^2
            for j in (i+1):n_p
                xpp = copy(x); xpp[i] += h[i]; xpp[j] += h[j]
                xpm = copy(x); xpm[i] += h[i]; xpm[j] -= h[j]
                xmp = copy(x); xmp[i] -= h[i]; xmp[j] += h[j]
                xmm = copy(x); xmm[i] -= h[i]; xmm[j] -= h[j]
                H[i, j] = H[j, i] =
                    (f(xpp) - f(xpm) - f(xmp) + f(xmm)) / (4 * h[i] * h[j])
            end
        end
        return H
    end
    H = _fd_hessian(nb_nll, p̂)
    V_oim = LinearAlgebra.inv(LinearAlgebra.Symmetric(H))
    # For `vce = :robust` / `:cluster`, build the sandwich vcov:
    #   V = A⁻¹ B A⁻¹ · correction
    # with A = OIM Hessian. B is the meat:
    #   robust : B = Σ_i s_i s_iᵀ                      (correction = n/(n-1))
    #   cluster: B = Σ_g (Σ_{i∈g} s_i)(Σ_{i∈g} s_i)ᵀ   (correction = G/(G-1))
    # Per-obs scores via central finite differences (gamma_inc-safe).
    V = if vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
        function nb_nll_i(p, i)
            β_l = p[1:k]; α_l = exp(p[k + 1])
            η_i  = LinearAlgebra.dot(view(Xm, i, :), β_l)
            μ_i  = exp(η_i); inv_α = 1 / α_l
            ll_i = SpecialFunctions.loggamma(yv[i] + inv_α) -
                   SpecialFunctions.loggamma(inv_α) -
                   SpecialFunctions.loggamma(yv[i] + 1) -
                   (yv[i] + inv_α) * log(1 + α_l * μ_i) +
                   yv[i] * log(α_l) + yv[i] * η_i
            return -ll_i
        end
        h_g  = sqrt(sqrt(eps(Float64))) .* max.(abs.(p̂), 1.0)
        # Per-obs score matrix S (n × (k+1)).
        S = zeros(n, k + 1)
        for i in 1:n, j in 1:(k + 1)
            xp = copy(p̂); xp[j] += h_g[j]
            xm = copy(p̂); xm[j] -= h_g[j]
            S[i, j] = (nb_nll_i(xp, i) - nb_nll_i(xm, i)) / (2 * h_g[j])
        end
        if vce == :robust
            B = S' * S
            V_oim * B * V_oim * (n / (n - 1))
        else
            cluster_var === nothing &&
                error("vce = :cluster requires `cluster_var = :varname`")
            cl = dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]
            B  = zeros(k + 1, k + 1)
            for g in unique(cl)
                sg = vec(sum(S[cl .== g, :], dims = 1))
                B .+= sg * sg'
            end
            G = length(unique(cl))
            V_oim * B * V_oim * (G / (G - 1))
        end
    else
        V_oim
    end
    se_full = sqrt.(max.(LinearAlgebra.diag(V), 0.0))
    se_β    = se_full[1:k]
    se_lnα  = se_full[k + 1]
    se_α    = α * se_lnα                   # delta method on exp(lnα)

    # CIs
    crit  = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 1 - (1-level)/2)
    z_β   = β̂ ./ se_β
    p_β   = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_β)))
    ci_lo_β = β̂ .- crit .* se_β
    ci_hi_β = β̂ .+ crit .* se_β
    lnα_lo, lnα_hi = lnα - crit*se_lnα, lnα + crit*se_lnα
    α_lo,   α_hi   = exp(lnα_lo),       exp(lnα_hi)

    # Null model (intercept-only NB) for pseudo R². Closed form for β:
    # β̂_0 = log(mean(y)). For α we do a 1D maximization (Nelder–Mead, no
    # autodiff — autodiff into `loggamma`/`gamma_inc` doesn't always have
    # ForwardDiff methods, so we keep the null fit derivative-free).
    ȳ      = Statistics.mean(yv)
    β0_null = log(ȳ)
    function nb_ll_null_α(α::Float64)
        μ = fill(ȳ, length(yv))
        inv_α = 1 / α
        sum(SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(yv .+ inv_α) .-
            SpecialFunctions.loggamma(inv_α) .-
            SpecialFunctions.loggamma.(yv .+ 1) .-
            (yv .+ inv_α) .* log.(1 .+ α .* μ) .+
            yv .* log(α) .+ yv .* β0_null)
    end
    res0 = _optimize_compat(α -> -nb_ll_null_α(exp(α[1])), [log(1.0)],
                          Optim.NelderMead())
    α̂_null   = exp(Float64(Optim.minimizer(res0)[1]))
    ll_null  = nb_ll_null_α(α̂_null)
    pseudo_r2 = 1 - ll / ll_null

    # LR chi2 (model vs intercept only) — NB likelihood ratio
    LR    = 2 * (ll - ll_null)
    LR_p  = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(k - 1), LR)

    # LR for α = 0 (NB vs Poisson). Half-mixture p-value: 0.5 · P(χ²₁ > LR)
    LR_α  = 2 * (ll - ll_pois)
    p_chibar = LR_α <= 0 ? 1.0 :
               0.5 * Distributions.ccdf(Distributions.Chisq(1), LR_α)

    # Stata `%9.0g` formatter (sign-aware, see `poisson_stata`)
    function g9(x; w::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
        (ismissing(x) || !isfinite(x)) && return lpad(".", w)
        sig_use = sig
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
        while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
            sig_use -= 1
            s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
        end
        0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
        lpad(s, w)
    end
    function commafmt(num)
        s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
        while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
        (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
    end

    # Wald chi² on slopes (used in robust header instead of LR).
    intercept_idx = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)
    slope_idx     = setdiff(1:k, [intercept_idx])
    Wald, Wald_p = NaN, NaN
    if !isempty(slope_idx)
        β_s = β̂[slope_idx]; V_s = V[slope_idx, slope_idx]
        Wald   = β_s' * LinearAlgebra.inv(V_s) * β_s
        Wald_p = 1 - Distributions.cdf(Distributions.Chisq(length(slope_idx)),
                                       Wald)
    end

    if !quiet
        println()
        # Header (`poisson`-style: title left, right column auto-sized)
        is_rob = vce == :robust || vce == :cluster
        nstr = commafmt(n)
        chi2_label = is_rob ? "Wald" : "LR"
        chi2_val   = is_rob ? Wald   : LR
        chi2_p     = is_rob ? Wald_p : LR_p
        wstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", chi2_val)
        pstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", chi2_p)
        rstr = Printf.@sprintf("%.4f", pseudo_r2)
        vw   = maximum(length, (nstr, wstr, pstr, rstr))
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %*s\n",
                       "Negative binomial regression", "Number of obs", vw, nstr)
        Printf.@printf("%56s%-13s = %*s\n", "",
                       "$chi2_label chi2($(length(slope_idx)))", vw, wstr)
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %*s\n",
                       "Dispersion: mean", "Prob > chi2", vw, pstr)
        ll_label = is_rob ? "Log pseudolikelihood" : "Log likelihood"
        Printf.@printf("%-56s%-13s = %*s\n",
                       Printf.@sprintf("%s = %.4f", ll_label, ll),
                       "Pseudo R2", vw, rstr)
        println()

        # Cluster sub-note (Stata: "(Std. err. adjusted for G clusters in <var>)").
        if vce == :cluster
            G = length(unique(dfc[!, Symbol(cluster_var)]))
            cl_str = Printf.@sprintf("(Std. err. adjusted for %s clusters in %s)",
                                     commafmt(G), cluster_var)
            println(lpad(cl_str, 78))
        end

        # Coefficient table — Stata order: slopes first, _cons last, then
        # /lnalpha and alpha.
        ord = intercept_idx === nothing ? collect(slope_idx) :
                                          vcat(slope_idx, [intercept_idx])
        println("-"^78)
        if is_rob
            println("             |               Robust")
        end
        se_label = is_rob ? "std. err." : "Std. err."
        Printf.@printf("%12s | Coefficient  %s      z    P>|z|     [%g%% conf. interval]\n",
                       string(formula.lhs), se_label, 100*level)
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        for i in ord
            label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
            Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                           label, g9(β̂[i]; w=10), g9(se_β[i]; w=9),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_β[i]),
                           Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_β[i]),
                           g9(ci_lo_β[i]; w=9), g9(ci_hi_β[i]; w=10))
        end
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s%26s%s  %s\n",
                       "/lnalpha", g9(lnα; w=10), g9(se_lnα; w=9), "",
                       g9(lnα_lo; w=9), g9(lnα_hi; w=10))
        println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
        Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s%26s%s  %s\n",
                       "alpha", g9(α; w=10), g9(se_α; w=9), "",
                       g9(α_lo; w=9), g9(α_hi; w=10))
        println("-"^78)
        # LR α=0 footer — only printed for OIM (Stata omits it under
        # `vce(robust)` because the LR test isn't valid under
        # misspecified likelihood).
        if !is_rob
            chibar_str = LR_α >= 1e4 ? Printf.@sprintf("%.1e", LR_α) :
                         Printf.@sprintf("%.2f", LR_α)
            Printf.@printf("LR test of alpha=0: chibar2(01) = %-15s Prob >= chibar2 = %.3f\n",
                           chibar_str, p_chibar)
        end
    end

    return (; model = m_pois, β_glm = β̂, V_glm = V[1:k, 1:k],
              coefnames_glm = cn,
              lnα, se_lnα, α, se_α,
              ll, ll_pois, ll_null, pseudo_r2,
              n, k, LR, LR_p, LR_α, p_chibar)
end
```

### 13.3.3 Bootstrap standard-errors example

```{julia}
#=
* Sample is only the first 50 observations of chapter 10 data
use musr/mus10data.dta
quietly keep if year02 == 1
quietly drop if _n > 50
quietly keep docvis chronic age 
quietly save musr/bootdata, replace
=#
# Use first 50 observations of year02 = 1 from the doctor visits data
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]
@printf("Bootstrap dataset: %d obs\n", DataFrames.nrow(df_boot))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Option vce(bootstrap) to compute bootstrap standard errors
poisson docvis chronic, vce(boot, reps(400) seed(10101) nodots)
=#
# Stata `poisson docvis chronic, vce(boot, reps(400) seed(10101) nodots)`.
# `poisson_boot_stata` (chunk 1) does the full Stata-format output:
# Number of obs / Replications / Wald chi2 / Log likelihood / Pseudo R²
# header, "Observed coefficient | Bootstrap std. err. | … | Normal-based CI"
# subheaders, slopes-first / _cons-last row order. Self-contained — loads
# df_boot here so the chunk runs without the §13.3.3 setup chunk above.
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]

poisson_boot_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                   B = 400, seed = 10101);
```

### 13.3.4 How many bootstraps?

```{julia}
#=
* Bootstrap standard errors for different reps and seeds
quietly poisson docvis chronic, vce(boot, reps(50) seed(10101))
estimates store boot50
quietly poisson docvis chronic, vce(boot, reps(50) seed(20202))
estimates store boot50diff
quietly poisson docvis chronic, vce(boot, reps(2000) seed(10101))
estimates store boot2000
quietly poisson docvis chronic, vce(robust)
estimates store robust
estimates table boot50 boot50diff boot2000 robust, b(%8.5f) se(%8.5f)
=#
# How sensitive are the bootstrap SEs to (a) the number of replications and
# (b) the RNG seed? Compare four estimators of `Var(β̂)` for the same point
# estimate β̂:
#   boot50      — B = 50,    seed = 10101
#   boot50diff  — B = 50,    seed = 20202   (different seed, same B)
#   boot2000    — B = 2000,  seed = 10101   (more reps, same seed as boot50)
#   robust      — sandwich (no bootstrap)
# Stata's `estimates table` lays them out side-by-side; we build the same
# comparison via four chunk-1 helper calls (`poisson_boot_stata`,
# `poisson_stata`) with `quiet = true`, then assemble the table.
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]

print("running boot50 (B=50, seed=10101)... ")
b50    = poisson_boot_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                            B = 50,   seed = 10101, quiet = true);  println("done")
print("running boot50diff (B=50, seed=20202)... ")
b50d   = poisson_boot_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                            B = 50,   seed = 20202, quiet = true);  println("done")
print("running boot2000 (B=2000, seed=10101)... ")
b2000  = poisson_boot_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                            B = 2000, seed = 10101, quiet = true);  println("done")
rob    = poisson_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                       vce = :robust, quiet = true)

# β̂ is the same across all four; only SEs differ.
β_disp  = b50.β   # GLM order: [_cons, chronic]
se_b50  = b50.se
se_b50d = b50d.se
se_b2k  = b2000.se
se_rob  = sqrt.(LinearAlgebra.diag(rob.V_glm))

cn = ["chronic", "_cons"]
i_chr = 2; i_con = 1   # GLM puts (Intercept) first

println("\n", "-"^65)
Printf.@printf("%12s | %10s %10s %10s %10s\n",
               "Variable", "boot50", "boot50diff", "boot2000", "robust")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^51)
for (lab, idx) in [("chronic", i_chr), ("_cons", i_con)]
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %10.5f %10.5f %10.5f %10.5f\n",
                   lab, β_disp[idx], β_disp[idx], β_disp[idx], β_disp[idx])
    Printf.@printf("%12s | (%8.5f) (%8.5f) (%8.5f) (%8.5f)\n",
                   "", se_b50[idx], se_b50d[idx], se_b2k[idx], se_rob[idx])
end
println("-"^65);
```

### 13.3.5 Clustered bootstraps

```{julia}
#=
* Option vce(boot, cluster) to compute cluster-bootstrap standard errors
poisson docvis chronic, vce(boot, cluster(age) reps(400) seed(10101) nodots)

poisson docvis chronic, vce(cluster age)
=#
# (1) Cluster bootstrap: `poisson_boot_stata(... cluster_var = :age)` resamples
#     the 26 unique age groups (panel_bootstrap), refits Poisson on each, and
#     prints the Stata header with "(Replications based on G clusters in age)".
# (2) Analytical cluster-robust SE: `poisson_stata(... vce = :cluster,
#     cluster_var = :age)` uses the CR1 sandwich
#         V = (G/(G-1))·(n-1)/(n-k)·A⁻¹·(Σ_g s_g s_g')·A⁻¹
#     where s_g aggregates the per-obs scores within each cluster and prints
#     "(Std. err. adjusted for G clusters in age)" — matching Stata's
#     `vce(cluster age)` output exactly.
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]

poisson_boot_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                   B = 400, seed = 10101, cluster_var = :age)

println()
poisson_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
              vce = :cluster, cluster_var = :age);
```

### 13.3.8 Bootstrap CI example

```{julia}
# Stata: `poisson docvis chronic, vce(boot, reps(999) seed(10101) bca);
# estat bootstrap, all` — all four bootstrap CI types side-by-side.
# `poisson_boot_ci_stata` (chunk 1) does the full pipeline:
#   1. Fit Poisson on full data → β̂
#   2. B = 999 obs-level bootstrap reps → β_boot matrix (for SE, P, BC, BCa)
#   3. Leave-one-out jackknife → β_jack matrix (for BCa acceleration `a`)
#   4. Print Observed coef / Bias / Bootstrap SE + four CI rows per coef
#      labelled (N), (P), (BC), (BCa)
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]

bs_fit = poisson_boot_ci_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                               B = 999, seed = 10101);
```

### 13.3.9 Bootstrap estimate of bias

```{julia}
#=
* List the average of the bootstraps
matrix list e(b_bs)
=#
# Stata's `e(b_bs)` is the mean of the bootstrap β-matrix across replicates,
# stored as a 1×k row matrix with equation-prefixed column names. Stata
# prints it as a Mata-style matrix block. We reproduce the format from the
# `bs_fit.β_boot` matrix saved in the §13.3.8 chunk above. Each column is
# Mean(β_boot[:, j]); the "docvis:" prefix is the dependent-variable label.
# bs_fit.β_boot stores coefficients in GLM order [(Intercept), chronic];
# Stata displays slopes first, then _cons.
β_bs    = vec(Statistics.mean(bs_fit.β_boot, dims = 1))
chronic = β_bs[2]; _cons = β_bs[1]
strip0(s) = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1.")
println()
println("e(b_bs)[1,2]")
println("       docvis:    docvis:")
println("      chronic      _cons")
@printf("y1  %9s  %9s\n",
        strip0(Printf.@sprintf("%.8f", chronic)),
        strip0(Printf.@sprintf("%.8f", _cons)))
```

### 13.4.2 Bootstrap of a parameter estimate

```{julia}
# Stata's `bootstrap, reps(400) seed(10101) nodots noheader: poisson docvis
# chronic` runs the same Poisson + bootstrap pipeline as `poisson docvis
# chronic, vce(boot, …)`, with `noheader` suppressing the regression-header
# block. `poisson_boot_stata(... noheader = true)` from chunk 1 prints just
# the coefficient table.
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]

poisson_boot_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                   B = 400, seed = 10101, noheader = true);
```

### 13.4.3 Bootstrap of a standard error

```{julia}
# `poisson_boot_b_se_stata` (chunk 1) bootstraps both β and the OIM SEs in
# one pass. Each resample refits Poisson, saves β̂ AND se(β̂), then we
# print Stata's two-block table:
#   - docvis    block: bootstrap of β
#   - docvis_se block: bootstrap of se(β)
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]

poisson_boot_b_se_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                        B = 400, seed = 10101);
```

### 13.4.4 Bootstrap of a user-written estimator

```{julia}
# Stata's `program poissrobust, eclass` is just a wrapper that fits Poisson
# with vce(robust) and stores e(b)/e(V). In Julia the helper does the same:
# `poisson_stata(... vce = :robust)` returns a NamedTuple with `β`, `V`,
# `coefnames` already in Stata-display order (slopes first, _cons last).
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]

# Step 1 — run the wrapper (full Stata-format table)
fit_pr = poisson_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                       vce = :robust)

# Step 2 — `ereturn display`: just the coefficient table, with capital
# "Std. err." (no "Robust" subheader) and a "docvis" equation banner row.
println("\n. ereturn display")
β    = fit_pr.β
V    = fit_pr.V
se   = fit_pr.se
crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 0.975)
z_v  = β ./ se
p_v  = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z_v)))
lo_v = β .- crit .* se
hi_v = β .+ crit .* se

g9 = function(x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
    s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
    cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
    sig_use = sig
    while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
        sig_use -= 1
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    end
    0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    lpad(s, w_)
end

println("-"^78)
println("             | Coefficient  Std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95% conf. interval]")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
Printf.@printf("%-12s |\n", string(GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic).lhs))
for i in eachindex(β)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                   fit_pr.coefnames[i],
                   g9(β[i]; w_=10), g9(se[i]; w_=9),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z_v[i]),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p_v[i]),
                   g9(lo_v[i]; w_=9), g9(hi_v[i]; w_=10))
end
println("-"^78)
```

### 13.4.5 Bootstrap of a two-step estimator

```{julia}
# Same as §13.4.3 but bootstraps the ROBUST sandwich SE (not the OIM SE).
# `poisson_boot_b_se_stata(... vce = :robust)` switches the per-resample
# SE computation to the n/(n-1)-corrected sandwich `(n/(n-1)) A⁻¹ B A⁻¹`,
# matching Stata's `poissrobust` program (which fits with `vce(robust)`).
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus10data.dta"))
df_boot = filter(r -> r.year02 == 1, df_boot)[1:50, [:docvis, :chronic, :age]]

poisson_boot_b_se_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                        B = 400, seed = 10101, vce = :robust);
```

```{julia}
# Heckman two-step on the mus16 ambulatory-expenditure data:
#   Stage 1: probit of dy = 1{y > 0} on xlist (selection)
#   Stage 2: OLS of ln(y) on xlist + invmills (where invmills = φ(x'γ̂)/Φ(x'γ̂))
# `probit_stata` (chunk 1) gives the Stata probit table; we then construct
# `invmills` from the probit linear index, restrict to y > 0, and run
# `regress_stata` for the outcome equation. Finally we print the
# `ereturn display` block — only the β column (no SEs since Stata posts
# `b` without `V`).
df16 = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus16data.dta"))
df16.y  = Float64.(df16.ambexp)
df16.dy = Int.(df16.y .> 0)
xs      = [:age, :female, :educ, :blhisp, :totchr, :ins]

# Stage 1 — probit on rows with non-missing dy + xs
df_pr = DataFrames.dropmissing(df16[:, vcat([:dy], xs)])
fml_p = StatsModels.term(:dy) ~ sum(StatsModels.term.(xs))
pr_fit = probit_stata(df_pr, fml_p)

# Stage 2 — compute invmills on the SAME df_pr rows (which we'll merge back
# to df16 by row position). Then build the OLS subsample on rows with y>0.
xb = GLM.modelmatrix(pr_fit.model) * pr_fit.β_glm
df_pr.invmills = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb) ./
                 Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb)
# Carry y over so we can filter to positives. df_pr was built from df16 via
# dropmissing on (:dy, xs); the same rows have a defined :y in df16.
df_pr.y = df16[
    DataFrames.completecases(df16[:, vcat([:dy], xs)]), :y]
df_pos = DataFrames.filter(r -> r.y > 0, df_pr)
df_pos.lny = log.(df_pos.y)

regress_stata(df_pos, :lny, vcat(xs, [:invmills]))

# `ereturn display` — Stata posts only β here (no V), so the table has just
# the Coefficient column.
m_out = FixedEffectModels.reg(df_pos,
    GLM.term(:lny) ~ sum(GLM.term.(vcat(xs, [:invmills]))))
β_out  = StatsBase.coef(m_out)
cn_out = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(m_out))
i_int  = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn_out)
slope  = setdiff(1:length(β_out), [i_int])
ord    = vcat(slope, [i_int])
labels = [cn_out[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn_out[i] for i in ord]

g9_e = function(x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
    s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
    cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
    sig_use = sig
    while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
        sig_use -= 1
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    end
    0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    lpad(s, w_)
end

println("\n. ereturn display")
println("-"^78)
println("             | Coefficient")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
for (lab, i) in zip(labels, ord)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s\n", lab, g9_e(β_out[i]; w_=10))
end
println("-"^78)
```

```{julia}
# Stata `heckman lny $xlist, select(dy = $xlist) twostep` — full Heckman
# (1979) two-step with first-stage-corrected SEs, σ, ρ, λ block.
# `heckman_twostep_stata` (chunk 1) handles the entire pipeline:
#   - probit on (dy ~ xs) → γ̂, λ_i, δ_i
#   - OLS on positives  → α̂ = (β̂, β̂_λ)
#   - σ̂² = (e'e)/n_2 + β̂_λ²·mean(δ_i)
#   - V(α̂) with first-stage correction:
#     V = σ̂²·(X*'X*)⁻¹·{X*'(I − ρ̂²Δ)X* + ρ̂²·X*'Δ·Z·Vγ·Z'Δ·X*}·(X*'X*)⁻¹
df16 = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus16data.dta"))
df16.y  = Float64.(df16.ambexp)
df16.dy = Int.(df16.y .> 0)
# Build `lny` with explicit `Int == 1` (defensive against `>` type-piracy
# from any loaded package). lny is missing for unselected rows.
df16.lny = Vector{Union{Missing, Float64}}(missing, DataFrames.nrow(df16))
for i in 1:DataFrames.nrow(df16)
    if Int(df16.dy[i]) == 1
        df16.lny[i] = log(Float64(df16.y[i]))
    end
end

xs      = [:age, :female, :educ, :blhisp, :totchr, :ins]
fml_out = StatsModels.term(:lny) ~ sum(StatsModels.term.(xs))
fml_sel = StatsModels.term(:dy)  ~ sum(StatsModels.term.(xs))

heckman_twostep_stata(df16, fml_out, fml_sel;
                     depvar_y = "lny", depvar_d = "dy");
```

### 13.4.6 Bootstrap Hausman test

```{julia}
#=
* Bootstrap for Heckman two-step estimator using chapter 16 example
bootstrap _b, reps(400) seed(10101) nodots nowarn: hecktwostep
=#
# Bootstrap of the full Heckman two-step pipeline. Stata's
# `bootstrap _b: hecktwostep` resamples observations from the FULL
# pre-stage-1 dataset, then runs the entire pipeline on each resample and
# saves the OLS β. We mirror that with `obs_bootstrap` (chunk 1) wrapping
# a closure that does both stages.
df16 = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus16data.dta"))
df16.y  = Float64.(df16.ambexp)
df16.dy = Int.(df16.y .> 0)
xs      = [:age, :female, :educ, :blhisp, :totchr, :ins]
df_h    = DataFrames.dropmissing(df16[:, vcat([:y, :dy], xs)])
fml_pr  = StatsModels.term(:dy)  ~ sum(StatsModels.term.(xs))
fml_ols = StatsModels.term(:lny) ~ sum(StatsModels.term.(vcat(xs, [:invmills])))

function _hecktwostep(d)
    m_pr = GLM.glm(fml_pr, d, Distributions.Binomial(), GLM.ProbitLink())
    xb   = GLM.modelmatrix(m_pr) * GLM.coef(m_pr)
    d2   = DataFrames.copy(d)
    d2.invmills = Distributions.pdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb) ./
                  Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), xb)
    # Filter to positives via plain Int equality (avoids any `>` issues)
    keep = Bool[Int(dy) == 1 for dy in d2.dy]
    d_pos = d2[keep, :]
    d_pos.lny = log.(Float64.(d_pos.y))
    return StatsBase.coef(FixedEffectModels.reg(d_pos, fml_ols))
end

# Observed (full-sample) β
β_hat  = _hecktwostep(df_h)
n_full = DataFrames.nrow(df_h)

print("running 400 reps... ")
t0 = time()
β_boot = obs_bootstrap(df_h; B = 400, seed = 10101, verbose = false) do d
    _hecktwostep(d)
end
@printf("done in %.2fs\n", time() - t0)

se_b = vec(Statistics.std(β_boot, dims = 1))
crit = Distributions.quantile(Distributions.Normal(), 0.975)
z    = β_hat ./ se_b
p    = 2 .* (1 .- Distributions.cdf.(Distributions.Normal(), abs.(z)))
lo   = β_hat .- crit .* se_b
hi   = β_hat .+ crit .* se_b

# Coefnames in OLS order: (Intercept), age, …, ins, invmills.
# Stata prints slopes first, _cons last.
cn  = ["(Intercept)", "age", "female", "educ", "blhisp", "totchr", "ins", "invmills"]
ord = vcat(2:length(cn), [1])

g9 = function(x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
    s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
    cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
    sig_use = sig
    while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
        sig_use -= 1
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    end
    0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    lpad(s, w_)
end
commafmt(num) = begin
    s = string(abs(num)); parts = String[]; i = length(s)
    while i >= 1; push!(parts, s[max(1, i-2):i]); i -= 3; end
    (num < 0 ? "-" : "") * join(reverse(parts), ",")
end

println()
Printf.@printf("%-59s%-13s = %5s\n",
               "Bootstrap results", "Number of obs", commafmt(n_full))
Printf.@printf("%59s%-13s = %5d\n", "", "Replications", 400)
println()
println("-"^78)
println("             |   Observed   Bootstrap                         Normal-based")
Printf.@printf("%12s | coefficient  std. err.      z    P>|z|     [95%% conf. interval]\n",
               "lny")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
for i in ord
    label = cn[i] == "(Intercept)" ? "_cons" : cn[i]
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s  %s  %s   %s    %s  %s\n",
                   label, g9(β_hat[i]; w_=10), g9(se_b[i]; w_=9),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%7.2f", z[i]),
                   Printf.@sprintf("%.3f", p[i]),
                   g9(lo[i]; w_=9), g9(hi[i]; w_=10))
end
println("-"^78);
```

```{julia}
#=
```
```{julia}
* Program to return (b1-b2) for hausman test of endogeneity
program hausmantest, eclass
  version 11
  tempname b bols biv
  regress ldrugexp hi_empunion totchr age female blhisp linc, vce(robust) 
  matrix `bols' = e(b)
  ivregress 2sls ldrugexp (hi_empunion = ssiratio) totchr age female blhisp linc, vce(robust)  
  matrix `biv' = e(b)
  matrix `b' = `bols' - `biv'
  ereturn post `b' 
end
=#
# Stata `program hausmantest` runs OLS and 2SLS on the same regressors
# (with `hi_empunion` instrumented by `ssiratio`), then posts the
# difference β̂_OLS − β̂_IV as the Hausman test statistic for endogeneity.
# In Julia we compose chunk-1 helpers `regress_stata` and `ivregress_2sls`
# (both Stata-format) and then print the difference table in `ereturn
# display` style.
df6 = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus06data.dta"))
xs6 = [:totchr, :age, :female, :blhisp, :linc]

# Stage 1 — OLS with vce(robust). Helper accepts a single endogenous-style
# regressor list; we put `hi_empunion` first to match Stata's coef ordering.
regress_stata(df6, :ldrugexp, vcat([:hi_empunion], xs6);
              vcov = FixedEffectModels.Vcov.robust(),
              noheader = true)

# Stage 2 — 2SLS with vce(robust). `first = false` suppresses the first-
# stage table (Stata's `hausmantest` doesn't show it).
ivregress_2sls(df6, :ldrugexp, :hi_empunion => :ssiratio, xs6;
               robust = true, first = false)

# Compute β̂_OLS − β̂_IV. We refit each model directly (the helpers above
# print but don't return) so we can grab the coefficients.
df6c = DataFrames.dropmissing(df6,
    [:ldrugexp, :hi_empunion, :ssiratio, :totchr, :age, :female, :blhisp, :linc])
m_ols = FixedEffectModels.reg(df6c,
    GLM.@formula(ldrugexp ~ hi_empunion + totchr + age + female + blhisp + linc),
    FixedEffectModels.Vcov.robust())
m_iv  = FixedEffectModels.reg(df6c,
    GLM.@formula(ldrugexp ~ totchr + age + female + blhisp + linc +
                 (hi_empunion ~ ssiratio)),
    FixedEffectModels.Vcov.robust())

cn_ols = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(m_ols))
cn_iv  = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(m_iv))
β_ols  = StatsBase.coef(m_ols)
β_iv   = StatsBase.coef(m_iv)
# Align by name: Stata's hausmantest order is hi_empunion, totchr, age,
# female, blhisp, linc, _cons.
labels = ["hi_empunion", "totchr", "age", "female", "blhisp", "linc", "_cons"]
function _lookup(cn, lab)
    target = lab == "_cons" ? "(Intercept)" : lab
    findfirst(==(target), cn)
end
diff_v = [β_ols[_lookup(cn_ols, l)] - β_iv[_lookup(cn_iv, l)] for l in labels]

g9_h = function(x; w_::Int=10, sig::Int=7)
    s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig, x)
    cap = (0 < abs(x) < 1 && x < 0) ? 10 : 9
    sig_use = sig
    while length(s) > cap && sig_use > 1
        sig_use -= 1
        s = Printf.@sprintf("%.*g", sig_use, x)
    end
    0 < abs(x) < 1 && (s = replace(s, r"^(-?)0\." => s"\1."))
    lpad(s, w_)
end

println("\n. ereturn display")
println("-"^78)
println("             | Coefficient")
println("-"^13, "+", "-"^64)
for (lab, d) in zip(labels, diff_v)
    Printf.@printf("%12s | %s\n", lab, g9_h(d; w_=10))
end
println("-"^78);
```

```{julia}
#=
// Following not included in book
* Check preceding program by running once
use musr/mus06data.dta, clear
hausmantest
ereturn display
=#
# Bootstrap of the Hausman test β̂_OLS − β̂_IV. Each resample refits both
# OLS and 2SLS on the resampled data, computes the difference vector, and
# stores it. Stata's `bootstrap _b: hausmantest` mirrors this exactly. We
# use `obs_bootstrap` (chunk 1) for resampling and `bootstrap_b_table_stata`
# (chunk 1) for the Stata-format output table.
df6 = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/mus06data.dta"))
df6c = DataFrames.dropmissing(df6,
    [:ldrugexp, :hi_empunion, :ssiratio, :totchr, :age, :female, :blhisp, :linc])

# Closure that runs the full hausmantest pipeline on a resampled df and
# returns β̂_OLS − β̂_IV as a Vector{Float64} aligned to `labels`.
labels = ["hi_empunion", "totchr", "age", "female", "blhisp", "linc", "_cons"]
fml_ols = GLM.@formula(ldrugexp ~ hi_empunion + totchr + age + female + blhisp + linc)
fml_iv  = GLM.@formula(ldrugexp ~ totchr + age + female + blhisp + linc +
                       (hi_empunion ~ ssiratio))

function _hausmantest(d)
    m_ols = FixedEffectModels.reg(d, fml_ols)
    m_iv  = FixedEffectModels.reg(d, fml_iv)
    cn_ols = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(m_ols))
    cn_iv  = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(m_iv))
    β_ols  = StatsBase.coef(m_ols); β_iv = StatsBase.coef(m_iv)
    function _lookup(cn, lab)
        target = lab == "_cons" ? "(Intercept)" : lab
        findfirst(==(target), cn)
    end
    return [β_ols[_lookup(cn_ols, l)] - β_iv[_lookup(cn_iv, l)] for l in labels]
end

# Observed difference vector
β_obs = _hausmantest(df6c)
n_obs = DataFrames.nrow(df6c)

print("running 400 reps... ")
t0 = time()
β_boot = obs_bootstrap(df6c; B = 400, seed = 10101, verbose = false) do d
    _hausmantest(d)
end
@printf("done in %.2fs\n", time() - t0)

bootstrap_b_table_stata(β_obs, β_boot, labels;
                        n_obs = n_obs, depvar = "");
```

```{julia}
# H0: β̂_OLS_hi_empunion − β̂_IV_hi_empunion = 0 using the bootstrap
# variance estimate. `test_stata` (chunk 1) accepts `β`, `V`, `coefnames`

# model object — `model = nothing`.
V_boot = Statistics.cov(β_boot)            # k×k bootstrap variance matrix
test_stata(nothing, "hi_empunion";
           β = β_obs, V = V_boot, coefnames = labels,
```

### 13.4.7 Bootstrap SE of the coefficient of variation

```{julia}
# Bootstrap of a SCALAR statistic — the coefficient of variation
# `coeffvar = std(docvis) / mean(docvis)` — computed on resamples of
# musr/bootdata. `obs_bootstrap` (chunk 1) handles the resampling; the
# closure returns a 1-element vector. `bootstrap_b_table_stata` (chunk 1)
# formats the output with Stata's optional sub-header showing
# "Command: …" and the named expression.
df_bd = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/bootdata.dta"))
n_bd  = DataFrames.nrow(df_bd)

# Closure: compute coefficient of variation of `docvis` on resampled data
function _coeffvar(d)
    y = Float64.(d.docvis)
    return [Statistics.std(y) / Statistics.mean(y)]
end

cv_obs = _coeffvar(df_bd)
print("running 400 reps... ")
t0 = time()
cv_boot = obs_bootstrap(df_bd; B = 400, seed = 10101, verbose = false) do d
    _coeffvar(d)
end
@printf("done in %.2fs\n", time() - t0)

# Persist the 400 replicates (Stata's `saving(musr/coeffofvar, replace)`).
mkpath("musr")
CSV.write("musr/coeffofvar.csv",
          DataFrames.DataFrame(coeffvar = vec(cv_boot)))

bootstrap_b_table_stata(cv_obs, cv_boot, ["coeffvar"];
                        n_obs = n_bd, depvar = "",
                        command = "summarize docvis",
                        expressions = ["coeffvar" => "r(sd)/r(mean)"]);
```

## 13.5 Bootstraps with asymptotic refinement

### 13.5.1 Percentile-t method

### 13.5.2 Percentile-t Wald test

```{julia}
#=
* Percentile-t for a single coefficient: Bootstrap the t statistic
use musr/bootdata, clear
quietly poisson docvis chronic, vce(robust)
local theta = _b[chronic] 
local setheta = _se[chronic]
bootstrap tstar=((_b[chronic]-`theta')/_se[chronic]), seed(10101)        ///
  reps(999) nodots saving(musr/percentilet, replace): poisson docvis chronic, ///
  vce(robust)
=#
# Percentile-t bootstrap for β_chronic via the chunk-1 helper
# `bootstrap_tstar_stata`. The helper handles the entire pipeline:
#   1. Fit Poisson, vce(robust) → (θ, σ_θ) on the full sample
#   2. Bootstrap t* = (β̂*_chronic − θ) / SE*_chronic over B = 999 resamples
#   3. Persist replicates to `musr/percentilet.csv`
#   4. Print Stata's `bootstrap … : poisson` table with Command/expression
#      sub-header
# Returns `(; β_orig, se_orig, tstars, B, n)`. Downstream §13.5.3 reads
# `β_orig`, `se_orig`, `tstars` to build the percentile-t CI.
df_boot = DataFrames.DataFrame(ReadStatTables.readstat("musr/bootdata.dta"))

ptres = bootstrap_tstar_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic), :chronic;
                              B        = 999,
                              seed     = 10101,
                              vce      = :robust,
                              command  = "poisson docvis chronic, vce(robust)",
                              save_csv = "musr/percentilet.csv")
β_orig  = ptres.β_orig
se_orig = ptres.se_orig
tstars  = ptres.tstars
```

```{julia}
#=
* Percentile-t p-value for symmetric two-sided Wald test of H0: theta = 0
use musr/percentilet, clear
quietly count if abs(`theta'/`setheta') < abs(tstar)
display "p-value = " r(N)/_N
=#
# Percentile-t two-sided Wald test of H0: θ = 0 using the bootstrap
# distribution of t*. `percentilet_pvalue_stata` (chunk 1) computes
#     p = (1/B) · Σ_b 1{|t*_b| > |t_obs|},  t_obs = β_orig / se_orig
# from the `tstars`, `β_orig`, `se_orig` produced by §13.5.2's
# `bootstrap_tstar_stata` call.
percentilet_pvalue_stata(tstars, β_orig, se_orig);
```

### 13.5.3 Percentile-t CI

```{julia}
#=
* Percentile-t critical values and confidence interval
_pctile tstar, p(2.5,97.5)
scalar lb = `theta' + r(r1)*`setheta'
scalar ub = `theta' + r(r2)*`setheta'
display "2.5 and 97.5 percentiles of t* distn: " r(r1) ", " r(r2) _n ///
    "95 percent percentile-t confidence interval is  (" lb ","  ub ")"
=#

# Percentile-t 95% CI from the `tstars` distribution and the original
# full-sample (β_orig, se_orig). `percentilet_ci_stata` (chunk 1) computes
#     [β_orig + q(α/2)·se_orig,  β_orig + q(1-α/2)·se_orig]
# and prints the two-line Stata display.
percentilet_ci_stata(tstars, β_orig, se_orig);
```

```{julia}
#=
use musr/bootdata, clear
nbreg docvis chronic
=#

# `df_boot` was loaded in §13.5.2 from musr/bootdata.dta. `nbreg_stata`
# (chunk 1) fits NB2 jointly in (β, lnα), prints the Stata header
# (LR chi2 / Pseudo R²), the coefficient table with /lnalpha and alpha
# rows, and the LR test of α=0 reported as chibar2(01).
nb_chronic = nbreg_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic));
```

## 13.6 Bootstrap pairs via custom resampling

### 13.6.1 Manual resampling helper

### 13.6.2 Custom bootstrap loop

```{julia}
#=
* Program to do one bootstrap replication
program onebootrep, rclass
  version 11
  drop _all
  use musr/bootdata
  bsample
  poisson docvis chronic, vce(robust)
  return scalar tstar = (_b[chronic]-$theta)/_se[chronic]
end

* Now do 999 bootstrap replications
use musr/bootdata, clear
quietly poisson docvis chronic, vce(robust)
global theta = _b[chronic]
global setheta = _se[chronic]
simulate tstar=r(tstar), seed(10101) reps(999) nodots  ///
  saving(musr/percentilet2, replace): onebootrep

* Analyze the results to get the p-value
use musr/percentilet2, clear
quietly count if abs($theta/$setheta) < abs(tstar)
display "p-value = " r(N)/_N
=#

# Same percentile-t pipeline as §13.5.2 but with Stata's `simulate` instead
# of `bootstrap`. `bootstrap_tstar_stata` (chunk 1) fits Poisson on the full
# sample, then resamples observations B=999 times and returns the t*
# distribution; `percentilet_pvalue_stata` (chunk 1) computes the
# symmetric two-sided p-value  P(|t*| > |t_obs|),  t_obs = β_orig/se_orig.
ptres2 = bootstrap_tstar_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic), :chronic;
                               B        = 999,
                               seed     = 10101,
                               vce      = :robust,
                               command  = "poisson docvis chronic, vce(robust)",
                               save_csv = "musr/percentilet2.csv",
                               quiet    = true)
percentilet_pvalue_stata(ptres2.tstars, ptres2.β_orig, ptres2.se_orig);
```

### 13.6.3 Bootstrap Monte Carlo exercise

```{julia}
#=
* Program to do one bootstrap of B replications
program mybootstrap, rclass
  use musr/bootdata, clear
  quietly poisson docvis chronic, vce(robust) 
  global theta = _b[chronic]
  global setheta = _se[chronic]
  simulate tstar=r(tstar), reps(999) nodots  ///
    saving(musr/percentilet2, replace): onebootrep
  use musr/percentilet2, clear
  quietly count if abs($theta/$setheta) < abs(tstar)
  return scalar pvalue =  r(N)/_N 
end 
=#
#=
* Program to do one bootstrap of B replications
program mybootstrap, rclass
  use musr/bootdata, clear
  quietly poisson docvis chronic, vce(robust)
  global theta = _b[chronic]
  global setheta = _se[chronic]
  simulate tstar=r(tstar), reps(999) nodots  ///
    saving(musr/percentilet2, replace): onebootrep
  use musr/percentilet2, clear
  quietly count if abs($theta/$setheta) < abs(tstar)
  return scalar pvalue =  r(N)/_N
end

* Check the program by running once
set seed 10101
mybootstrap
display r(pvalue)
=#

# `mybootstrap_stata` (chunk 1) wraps the full §13.6.2 percentile-t pipeline
# into one call that returns the symmetric two-sided Wald p-value. Designed
# to be re-runnable with different seeds (used in the Monte-Carlo follow-up
# below). Mirrors Stata's `set seed 10101; mybootstrap; display r(pvalue)`.
mb_one = mybootstrap_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic), :chronic;
                            B    = 999,
                            seed = 10101,
                            vce  = :robust);
```

## 13.7 Alternative resampling schemes

### 13.7.1 Bootstrap pairs

```{julia}
#=
* Program to resample using bootstrap pairs
program bootpairs
  version 11 
  drop _all
  use musr/bootdata
  bsample
  poisson docvis chronic
end
=#
#=
* Program to resample using bootstrap pairs
program bootpairs
  version 11
  drop _all
  use musr/bootdata
  bsample
  poisson docvis chronic
end

* Check the program by running once
bootpairs
=#

# `bsample_stata` (chunk 1) is Stata's `bsample` — observation-level resample
# with replacement. Then `poisson_stata` with `vce=:oim` matches Stata's
# default `poisson docvis chronic` (no robust/cluster — uses the OIM SEs).
# RNG note: Julia's MersenneTwister differs from Stata's MT64, so the
# resampled rows — and the resulting coefficients — will not match Stata's
# exact "one run" output (Coefficient = 1.305169, etc.).
poisson_stata(bsample_stata(df_boot; seed = 10101),
              GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
              vce = :oim);
```

```{julia}
#=
* Check the program by running once
bootpairs
=#
#=
* Bootstrap pairs for the parameters
simulate _b, seed(10101) reps(400) nodots: bootpairs
summarize
=#

# `simulate _b, reps(400): bootpairs` runs the §13.7.1 bootstrap-pair program
# 400 times and saves the coefficient vector each time, then `summarize`
# reports univariate stats for `_b_chronic` / `_b_cons`. `obs_bootstrap`
# (chunk 1) does the resampling loop, and `summarize_stata` (chunk 1)
# prints the Stata-style summary table.
# RNG note: Julia's MersenneTwister differs from Stata's MT64, so the
# 400 resamples — and thus their summary statistics — will not match
# Stata's exact numbers. The means should be close to the full-sample β.
β_pairs_mat = obs_bootstrap(df_boot; B = 400, seed = 10101, verbose = false) do d
    fit = poisson_stata(d, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                        vce = :oim, quiet = true)
    return [fit.β_glm[findfirst(==("chronic"),     fit.coefnames_glm)],
            fit.β_glm[findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), fit.coefnames_glm)]]
end

df_pairs = DataFrames.DataFrame(:_b_chronic => β_pairs_mat[:, 1],
                                :_b_cons    => β_pairs_mat[:, 2])
summarize_stata(df_pairs);
```

```{julia}
#=
* Bootstrap pairs for the parameters
simulate _b, seed(10101) reps(400) nodots: bootpairs
summarize
=#
#=
// Following not included in book
* Compare to bootstrap command
use musr/bootdata, clear
bootstrap, reps(100) seed(10101): poisson docvis chronic
=#

# Stata's `bootstrap _b: poisson docvis chronic` — observation-level
# bootstrap of the Poisson coefficients. `obs_bootstrap` (chunk 1) does
# the resampling loop returning [chronic, _cons] per replicate, and
# `bootstrap_b_table_stata` (chunk 1) prints the Stata-style header
# (Bootstrap results / Number of obs / Replications / Command) and the
# Normal-based CI table. Layout matches Stata; numbers differ due to the
# MersenneTwister vs MT64 RNG.
fit0_b = poisson_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                       vce = :oim, quiet = true)
i_chr  = findfirst(==("chronic"),     fit0_b.coefnames_glm)
i_cons = findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), fit0_b.coefnames_glm)

β_boot100 = obs_bootstrap(df_boot; B = 100, seed = 10101, verbose = false) do d
    fit = poisson_stata(d, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                        vce = :oim, quiet = true)
    return [fit.β_glm[findfirst(==("chronic"),     fit.coefnames_glm)],
            fit.β_glm[findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), fit.coefnames_glm)]]
end

bootstrap_b_table_stata([fit0_b.β_glm[i_chr], fit0_b.β_glm[i_cons]],
                        β_boot100, ["chronic", "_cons"];
                        n_obs   = DataFrames.nrow(df_boot),
                        depvar  = "docvis",
                        command = "poisson docvis chronic");
```

### 13.7.2 Parametric bootstrap

```{julia}
#=
* Estimate the model with original actual data and save estimates
use musr/bootdata
nbreg docvis chronic
predict muhat
global alpha = e(alpha)
=#
#=
* Estimate the model with original actual data and save estimates
use musr/bootdata
nbreg docvis chronic
predict muhat
global alpha = e(alpha)
=#

# Original-data NB fit and saved quantities (μ̂, α) used downstream by the
# parametric bootstrap. `nbreg_stata` (chunk 1) fits NB2 jointly in (β, lnα)
# and prints the full Stata table including `/lnalpha`, `alpha`, and the
# `LR test of alpha=0: chibar2(01)` line.
nb_boot = nbreg_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic))

# Stata `predict muhat` after `nbreg` — conditional mean μ̂_i = exp(x_iᵀβ̂).
muhat = exp.(GLM.modelmatrix(nb_boot.model) * nb_boot.β_glm)
alpha = nb_boot.α
@printf("alpha = %.6f   mean(muhat) = %.6f\n", alpha, Statistics.mean(muhat))
```

```{julia}
#=
* Program for parametric bootstrap generating from negative binomial
program bootparametric, eclass
  version 11
  capture drop nu dvhat
  generate nu = rgamma(1/$alpha,$alpha)
  generate dvhat = rpoisson(muhat*nu)
  nbreg dvhat chronic
end
=#
#=
* Program for parametric bootstrap generating from negative binomial
program bootparametric, eclass
  version 11
  capture drop nu dvhat
  generate nu = rgamma(1/$alpha,$alpha)
  generate dvhat = rpoisson(muhat*nu)
  nbreg dvhat chronic
end

// Following not included in book
* Check the program by running once
set seed 10101
bootparametric
=#

# `bootparametric_nb_stata` (chunk 1) is the Julia equivalent of Stata's
# `bootparametric` program: draws ν ~ Gamma(1/α, α), y* ~ Poisson(μ̂·ν),
# overwrites `dvhat` in a copy of df_boot, and refits NB2 of dvhat on
# chronic — all in one call. Mirrors `set seed 10101; bootparametric`.
nb_par_one = bootparametric_nb_stata(df_boot, muhat, alpha,
                                      GLM.@formula(dvhat ~ chronic);
                                      seed = 10101);
```

```{julia}
#=
// Following not included in book 
* Check the program by running once
set seed 10101
bootparametric
=#
#=
* Parametric bootstrap for the parameters
simulate _b, seed(10101) reps(400) nodots: bootparametric
summarize
=#

# `simulate _b, reps(400) seed(10101): bootparametric` — runs the §13.7.2
# parametric NB2 program 400 times saving the coefficient vector each rep,
# then summarizes. Seed the global RNG once and let
# `bootparametric_nb_stata` (chunk 1) advance it; collect (β_chronic,
# β_cons, lnα) per replicate. RNG note: Julia's MersenneTwister differs
# from Stata's MT64, so summary stats won't match Stata exactly.
Random.seed!(10101)
β_par_mat = reduce(hcat, [
    let f = bootparametric_nb_stata(df_boot, muhat, alpha,
                                     GLM.@formula(dvhat ~ chronic);
                                     quiet = true)
        [f.β_glm[findfirst(==("chronic"),     f.coefnames_glm)],
         f.β_glm[findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), f.coefnames_glm)],
         f.lnα]
    end
    for _ in 1:400])'

df_par = DataFrames.DataFrame(:_b_chronic  => β_par_mat[:, 1],
                              :_b_cons     => β_par_mat[:, 2],
                              :_b_lnalpha  => β_par_mat[:, 3])
summarize_stata(df_par);
```

```{julia}
end

// Following not included in book
* Check the program by running once
bootresidual
=#

# `bootresidual_ols_stata` (chunk 1) mirrors Stata's `bootresidual`
# program: fits OLS on bootdata (table 1), resamples residuals with
# replacement, builds y* = X β̂ + u*, refits y* on chronic (table 2),
# and prints both `regress` tables plus the `(option xb assumed; fitted
# values)` notice between them. RNG note: the original-data table
# (chronic = 4.694444, etc.) matches Stata exactly; the bootstrap
# table's coefficients differ since Julia's MersenneTwister ≠ Stata's
# MT64.
bootresidual_ols_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                       seed = 10101);
```

```{julia}
#=
// Following not included in book 
* Check the program by running once
bootresidual
=#
#=
* Residual bootstrap for the parameters
simulate _b, seed(10101) reps(400) nodots: bootresidual
summarize
=#

# `simulate _b, reps(400) seed(10101): bootresidual` — runs the §13.7.3
# residual-bootstrap program 400 times saving β̂ each rep, then summarizes.
# Seed the global RNG once and let `bootresidual_ols_stata` (chunk 1)
# advance it; collect (β_chronic, β_cons) per replicate. RNG note: Julia's
# MersenneTwister differs from Stata's MT64, so summary stats won't match
# Stata exactly.
Random.seed!(10101)
β_res_mat = reduce(hcat, [
    let res = bootresidual_ols_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic);
                                      quiet = true)
        cn = string.(StatsBase.coefnames(res.boot))
        β  = FixedEffectModels.coef(res.boot)
        [β[findfirst(==("chronic"),     cn)],
         β[findfirst(==("(Intercept)"), cn)]]
    end
    for _ in 1:400])'

df_res = DataFrames.DataFrame(:_b_chronic => β_res_mat[:, 1],
                              :_b_cons    => β_res_mat[:, 2])
summarize_stata(df_res);
```

## 13.8 The jackknife

### 13.8.1 Jackknife method

### 13.8.2 Jackknife in Julia

```{julia}
#=
* Jackknife estimate of standard errors
use musr/bootdata, replace
poisson docvis chronic, vce(jackknife, mse nodots)
=#

# `poisson_jackknife_stata` (chunk 1) computes Stata's
# `vce(jackknife, mse)` SE: refits Poisson on each leave-one-out subset,
# then  V_jack = (n-1)/n · Σ (β̂_(i) − β̂)(β̂_(i) − β̂)ᵀ
# (centered on β̂ because of the `mse` option). Inference uses t with
# df = n − 1; the omnibus stat is `F(k, n − 1)`. The full Stata table
# (Number of obs / Replications / F / Prob > F / Log likelihood /
# Pseudo R² + the `Jackknife` sub-banner) is printed by the helper.
poisson_jackknife_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic));
```

```{julia}
#=
// Following not included in book
jacknife, mse nodots: poisson docvis chronic
=#

# Same as the previous chunk: `jackknife, mse nodots: poisson` is just
# the prefix-style equivalent of `poisson ..., vce(jackknife, mse nodots)`.
# `poisson_jackknife_stata` (chunk 1) handles both forms identically.
poisson_jackknife_stata(df_boot, GLM.@formula(docvis ~ chronic));
```
